s184a4b645b.summary: arXiv:2611.28638v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Retrieval-augmented language models answer well when the relevant document comes first or last and poorly when it sits in the middle.

sf73a5ed171.title: The Evaluation Substrate Matters: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Serving Substrates
sf73a5ed171.description: arXiv:2611.28671v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) usually coordinate heterogeneous models and tools to solve complex tasks, creating a growing need for reliable evaluation. However, a multi-agent workflow that is fastest in one serving environment can lose its advantage in another, even when its models, prompts, and task remain fixed. This makes a benchmark result conditional on how the workflow is executed. We introduce MASSys, a benchmark for measuring this dependence in multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems. MASSys executes the same candidate-task pairs across serving substrates and load regimes, using five workload families spanning software repair, research synthesis, financial analysis, interactive control, and diagram generation. It records task qu
sf73a5ed171.summary: arXiv:2611.28671v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) usually coordinate heterogeneous models and tools to solve complex tasks, creating a growing need for reliable evaluation.

s6894f63443.title: PopMelodyGen: A Copyright-Aware Platform for Controllable Pop-Melody Generation
s6894f63443.description: arXiv:2611.28686v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large-scale redistributable symbolic pop-melody data remain scarce due to copyright restrictions, creating a bottleneck for both practical deployment and reproducible research in music generation. We present PopMelodyGen, a copyright-aware platform for controllable pop-melody generation that combines rule-based synthesis with neural generation. Our approach first uses an expert synthesizer to produce large-scale labeled synthetic melodies from explicit musical knowledge and templates, providing scalable pretraining data with auditable provenance. A neural model is then pretrained on this corpus and adapted with a small licensed real-pop corpus to improve melodic naturalness while preserving controllability. The platform supports interactive
s6894f63443.summary: arXiv:2611.28686v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large-scale redistributable symbolic pop-melody data remain scarce due to copyright restrictions, creating a bottleneck for both practical deployment and reproducible…

s9368bf0ac1.title: SkillLens: An Interactive Human-LLM System for Diagnosing and Refining Agent Skills
s9368bf0ac1.description: arXiv:2611.28706v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM agents increasingly rely on reusable skills, yet maintaining them requires developers to connect revisions with changes in behavior and task outcomes. Existing workflows fragment evidence across versions, evaluation cases, and execution traces. We present SkillLens, an interactive human-LLM system for diagnosing and refining agent skills. A formative study with five developers and researchers identified challenges in prioritizing failures, reconstructing case-level evidence, and preserving context across revisions. SkillLens links performance changes, case transitions, skill diffs, invocation sequences, traces, and outputs in a recoverable workflow, while keeping model-generated explanations and refinements under human review. Through a
s9368bf0ac1.summary: arXiv:2611.28706v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM agents increasingly rely on reusable skills, yet maintaining them requires developers to connect revisions with changes in behavior and task outcomes.

se2fcf3c27d.title: KMed-31B Technical Report
se2fcf3c27d.description: arXiv:2611.28719v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present KMed-31B, a medical large language model post-trained from an open-weight model for on-premises deployment with limited hardware. Post-training a model for diverse medical tasks remains difficult, because improving one kind of task can lower performance on another. We attribute this to differences between tasks in expected output and available feedback. Medical question answering and diagnosis prediction have reference answers, whereas clinical inquiry has no single correct response and is judged with rubrics. We therefore divide medical training tasks into four categories by these two properties, train one specialist per category with a reward that its feedback supports, and integrate the specialists into a single student with M
se2fcf3c27d.summary: arXiv:2611.28719v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present KMed-31B, a medical large language model post-trained from an open-weight model for on-premises deployment with limited hardware.

s5fd56e1839.title: AERIN: Aerial Instance Navigation with a Visual World Model
s5fd56e1839.description: arXiv:2611.28723v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Searching from high altitude and navigating to a target instance specified by a reference image is a common application for UAVs. In such tasks, high-altitude observations provide broad ground coverage for efficient search, but targets occupy fewer pixels, making instance verification and action selection more difficult. We present AERIN, a visual world model that uses action-conditioned prediction to guide the UAV toward the target while adjusting its viewpoint to obtain higherquality observations for subsequent instance verification. Highaltitude navigation requires fine-grained target details and scene context relevant to visibility, but repeatedly predicting dense visual representations of this information is computationally expensive.
s5fd56e1839.summary: arXiv:2611.28723v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Searching from high altitude and navigating to a target instance specified by a reference image is a common application for UAVs.

s7c3b944c2e.title: Seeing Is Not Planning: Spatiotemporal Planning and Plan Repair in Multimodal LLMs
s7c3b944c2e.description: arXiv:2611.28726v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Planning in a visual world means reading the layout, foreseeing how the state will change, and following the task rules all at once. When a plan fails, a model should also use what went wrong to fix it. We call these two abilities spatiotemporal planning and plan repair, and test them with Railbound-Bench. A model sees a railway puzzle, adds tracks under a budget, and submits one complete layout; a simulator then moves all cars at once and decides whether the layout works. After a failure, the model sees what happened and may submit a new layout, up to five attempts in total. On the 200-puzzle main set, the best of nine models solves 59.5% within five attempts, the next 39.5%, and the other seven at most 10.0%; a 1,000-puzzle extended set w
s7c3b944c2e.summary: arXiv:2611.28726v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Planning in a visual world means reading the layout, foreseeing how the state will change, and following the task rules all at once.

sc1c847998c.title: Entangle: Scaling Human-Video In-Context World-Action Models across Unseen Tasks and Contexts
sc1c847998c.description: arXiv:2611.28732v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In-context learning (ICL) enables foundation models to perform unseen tasks from context without parameter updates. In robotic manipulation, a human video provides the context that specifies how a task should be performed. However, scaling human-video ICL on world-action models (WAMs) faces two challenges: task-level human-robot pairs are not temporally aligned with robot actions, and standard action losses allow policies to rely on initial-scene or task-identity shortcuts rather than tracking the context. We present Entangle, an in-context world-action model that maps a single human video and current robot observations to future visual states and executable actions. To scale temporally aligned training data, we convert recorded robot video
sc1c847998c.summary: Researchers present Entangle, an in-context world-action model for scaling human-video context to robot manipulation on unseen tasks.
sc1c847998c.why: Shows a route to teaching robots new tasks from human demo videos without retraining, though the abstract alone gives limited detail on results.

s107d0734a7.title: Multimodal LLMs Know the Game but Assume the Real World
s107d0734a7.description: arXiv:2611.28745v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal large language models can state the rules of a video game, but do they apply them when they only see the game? We introduce RuleCraft, 1,240 image questions over 155 Minecraft rules with outcomes verified in the game engine, each asked in text, on the image with the game named, and on the bare image. Six widely used models know the rules and recognize the game, yet answer the bare image by real-world physics: naming the game raises their accuracy on rules where the game departs from reality by 8.2-19.8 points on a main set and by 33.8-52.7 on a hard stress-test set. Their errors pick the real-world outcome, the gap is largest where the game leaves a scene unchanged, and reasoning traces state the game's rule, then answer by reali
s107d0734a7.summary: Researchers introduce RuleCraft, a benchmark showing multimodal LLMs know Minecraft rules but default to real-world physics when shown only the game image.
s107d0734a7.why: Highlights that multimodal models may fail to apply domain-specific rules from images, a risk for visual agents operating in non-realistic environments.

s0e46118066.title: Pretraining Representation Lottery Determines Fine-tuning Generalization
s0e46118066.description: arXiv:2611.28777v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large scale pretraining (PT) followed by fine-tuning (FT) is the central paradigm of modern deep learning, yet how PT shapes FT generalization remains poorly understood. We use a synthetic setup in which the ground-truth concept geometry of entities is known, as a controlled testbed to study how representational geometry affects model behavior and how PT representations determine FT generalization. We first show that models differing only in training seed can closely match in PT loss yet vary substantially in FT generalization. We hypothesize that a representational lottery underlies this phenomenon: the random seed dependent geometry formed during PT determines what FT can reach. We confirm this causally. First, injecting the ground-truth
s0e46118066.summary: A paper argues that pretraining representation differences, even from seed alone, largely determine how well models generalize after fine-tuning, using a synthetic testbed.
s0e46118066.why: Suggests fine-tuning outcomes can vary substantially between runs with similar pretraining loss, complicating reproducibility and model selection.

s4c9ef3f78b.title: HighwayVerse: A Chain-of-Inspection Benchmark for Highway Infrastructure Anomaly Understanding
s4c9ef3f78b.description: arXiv:2611.28800v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Practical highway infrastructure inspection entails progressive diagnostic reasoning from visual perception to maintenance decisions, yet existing benchmarks remain confined to isolated tasks, leaving Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) insufficiently evaluated across sequential inspection stages. Meanwhile, current datasets focus primarily on highway pavement defects, falling short of real-world inspection across diverse infrastructure components such as highway pavements, guardrails, glare screens, and drainage systems. To address these gaps, we formulate the Highway Infrastructure Inspection Progression Chain (HIIP-Chain), spanning Anomaly Detection, Anomaly Recognition, Condition Analysis, and Maintenance Resolution, and introduce
s4c9ef3f78b.summary: Researchers release HighwayVerse, a benchmark testing multimodal LLMs on sequential highway inspection tasks across pavements, guardrails, glare screens, and drainage.
s4c9ef3f78b.why: Offers a multi-stage evaluation for applying MLLMs to infrastructure inspection, though the abstract gives no performance findings.

s2336b28038.title: Not All Directions Are Flat: Decomposed-Gradient Flatness for Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Splatting
s2336b28038.description: arXiv:2611.28802v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many applications of novel view synthesis, such as augmented reality and robotics, can afford only a few input views, since dense capture is costly. With such sparse views, however, 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) overfits the training views and degrades at unseen viewpoints. Among the approaches to this problem, flat-minima optimization treats the Gaussians as trainable parameters and steers training toward flat minima, which generalize better, by perturbing the Gaussians with random noise or along the training gradient. However, these perturbations ignore their direction relative to the other training views. Interestingly, we find that the direction of the perturbation determines whether it improves generalization. Specifically, we decompose
s2336b28038.summary: A paper proposes decomposed-gradient flatness to improve sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting, reducing overfitting to training views.
s2336b28038.why: Targets a practical limitation for AR and robotics where only a few input views are available, but the abstract gives limited detail.

s97ac85659a.title: PointNeXt Adapter Improved Model for BIM Component Defect Association under Construction Images and Design Model Attributes
s97ac85659a.description: arXiv:2611.28820v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Construction site defect analysis increasingly requires linking field evidence to the correct BIM object, because a crack, spalling area, missing sleeve or misaligned support is useful for quality control only when it is connected with component identity, location, responsibility and design intent. This paper proposes a PointNeXt Adapter improved model for BIM component defect association under construction images and design model attributes. The method aligns site image crops, local point cloud patches, BIM component identifiers, geometry attributes, material categories, installation stage, inspection distance, viewpoint quality and source reliability tags into component level inspection windows. PointNeXt learns local geometry and deviati
s97ac85659a.summary: Researchers propose a PointNeXt Adapter model that links construction site images and point cloud patches to BIM components for defect association.
s97ac85659a.why: Could help construction tech teams tie field defects to the correct BIM objects for quality control, based on a research prototype.

sc95e0c5698.title: When Being Wrong Is Right: Reverse-Capability Audio CAPTCHAs through Psychoacoustic Design
sc95e0c5698.description: arXiv:2611.28823v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large audio-language models (LALMs) have recently been shown to bypass audio CAPTCHAs designed around limitations of automatic speech recognition. To address this threat, we introduce reverse-capability verification, a general CAPTCHA framework that reverses the conventional human-easy, machine-hard relationship with respect to the physical ground truth. It selects challenges in which stable human perceptual limitations cause the human-reference answer to differ from the physical ground truth, while machine analysis tends toward that truth. Because the verifier accepts the human-reference answer, advanced solver capabilities and resulting improved recovery of the physical ground truth may instead strengthen the human-machine separation. We
sc95e0c5698.summary: Researchers propose reverse-capability audio CAPTCHAs that exploit human perceptual limits so that humans answer differently from physical ground truth while machines do not.
sc95e0c5698.why: Offers a defense against large audio-language models bypassing audio CAPTCHAs, relevant to teams running bot protection.

sfcc2512e40.title: Hidden Sensitivity in LLM Pre-training: A Dynamic System View
sfcc2512e40.description: arXiv:2611.28830v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In Large Language Model (LLM) pre-training, loss curves can conceal substantial instability, i.e., even small perturbations may lead to dramatically different predictions while leaving loss nearly unchanged. To investigate this phenomenon and reveal the underlying mechanisms, we first formulate LLM pre-training as a non-autonomous dynamical system that jointly evolves model weights and Adam optimizer states. Based on this formulation, we introduce a normalized sensitivity score in optimizer-relative coordinates to identify sensitive training checkpoints. At one such checkpoint, a weight perturbation of only 10^(-5) leads to 35.7% disagreement in top-1 predictions and 16.2% disagreement in benchmark answers after 200 training steps, with onl
sfcc2512e40.summary: A paper frames LLM pretraining as a dynamical system and introduces a sensitivity score showing small perturbations can change predictions while loss barely moves.
sfcc2512e40.why: Reveals hidden training instability that loss curves miss, which matters for teams monitoring large pretraining runs.

s0e0564f762.title: Operational Assurance for LLM-Based Systems under Governance Opacity
s0e0564f762.description: arXiv:2611.28834v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the contemporary artificial intelligence ecosystem, foundation models are increasingly deployed under AI-as-a-Service (AIaaS) schemes characterized by high technical opacity, technological concentration, and limited external auditing capability over governance, training, and internal operational processes. Under these conditions, traditional ethical oversight approaches that focus exclusively on corporate governance or on internal model inspection become insufficient to ensure effective control over AI systems deployed in real-world contexts. This work proposes a pragmatic operational assurance framework inspired by Zero-Trust principles from cybersecurity, which shifts effective auditing efforts toward the application layer, where risk
s0e0564f762.summary: A paper proposes operational assurance methods for LLM-based systems deployed as AI-as-a-Service, where governance and training are opaque and external auditing is limited.
s0e0564f762.why: Addresses oversight of third-party foundation models that enterprises deploy without visibility into internal processes.

sbf287b64aa.title: KineState-SWAM: A Surgical World Action Model with Explicit Kinematics and Causal Interaction Dynamics
sbf287b64aa.description: arXiv:2611.28871v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Existing surgical world models often leave implicit how instrument motion drives localized tissue responses and how interaction history informs subsequent actions. We introduce KineState-SWAM, a surgical world-action model coupling action prediction and video generation through a persistent interaction state, separating kinematically determined instrument motion from learned scene evolution. A flow-matching policy predicts joint trajectories conditioned on interaction state, robot configuration, and task instruction. Kinematic Geometry Conditioning converts these trajectories into surface-motion tokens and spatially aligned instrument renderings using calibrated URDF kinematics. Causal Interaction Dynamics recurrently updates the state thro
sbf287b64aa.summary: Researchers introduce KineState-SWAM, a surgical world-action model that couples kinematic instrument motion with video generation through a persistent interaction state.
sbf287b64aa.why: Suggests more structured surgical robotics world models, though the abstract provides no benchmark outcomes.

s4d6451c050.title: NAT: Scaling Causal Neural Action Tokenizers Across Embodiments
s4d6451c050.description: arXiv:2611.28873v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Action tokenizers let robot policies treat control as autoregressive next-token prediction. As these policies are trained on larger and more diverse datasets, they will need a universal tokenizer that can encode actions from many embodiments and data sources, including ones it has not seen. We study action tokenization at scale, training on 49k hours of action data from real-world robots, handheld grippers, simulation, and humans. We introduce Neural Action Tokenizer (NAT), a causal tokenizer whose decoder lets actions be executed as their tokens are generated. Across four simulation benchmarks, NAT outperforms FAST and prior neural action tokenizers when tokenizing unseen robot embodiments, and in vision-language-action models it outperfor
s4d6451c050.summary: Researchers present NAT, a causal neural action tokenizer trained on 49k hours of action data across robots, grippers, simulation, and humans to handle many embodiments.
s4d6451c050.why: A universal action tokenizer could simplify training robot policies across heterogeneous hardware and data sources.

s7e0c27b696.title: Topological Neural Collapse
s7e0c27b696.description: arXiv:2611.28894v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neural collapse (NC) predicts that, late in training, last-layer class features concentrate at their means and the means form a simplex equiangular tight frame (ETF). We ask whether NC also leaves a signature in the functional connectome of each layer: the graph of Pearson correlations between hidden-unit activations, built per class and summarized by persistent graph homology. Using deep MLPs, we observe two topological phenomena that co-occur with the well-studied geometric NC in the final layers during the terminal phase. Contrary to NC1, the split-half variability of a class connectome increases (TNC1). The mean pairwise $H_0$ distance $\bar{D}$ between class connectomes also rises (TNC2), but unevenly across class pairs, unlike the equ
s7e0c27b696.summary: A paper reports topological signatures in the functional connectome of deep MLP layers that co-occur with neural collapse in final layers.
s7e0c27b696.why: Offers an analytical lens on internal network structure during training, with limited direct implications for engineering practice.

s5da93a4b8f.title: Can Open LLMs Clear Sanctions-Screening Alerts? A Pre-registered Test on Public Sanctions Lists with Turkish Name Variants
s5da93a4b8f.description: arXiv:2611.28914v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Sanctions screening raises name-based alerts that are mostly false positives, and level-1 analysts clear them by checking the customer's date of birth and name against a written policy. We test whether open-weight language models that a bank can run on its own premises can perform this level-1 disposition. From the UK and EU sanctions lists (7,103 natural persons) we built 12,200 synthetic customers: listed persons under six name conditions, including Turkish spellings of Arabic-origin names and Turkish romanisations of Cyrillic names, and two date-of-birth conditions, plus namesakes, near-name customers and a general population. A deterministic fuzzy and embedding screen raised 7,383 alerts, which three open models served on domestic infra
s5da93a4b8f.summary: A pre-registered study tests whether open-weight LLMs can clear sanctions-screening alerts using UK and EU lists with Turkish name variants.
s5da93a4b8f.why: Bears on whether banks can run compliance screening on-premises with open models, though the abstract does not report final results.

saa2e5088fa.title: Definition-Guided In-Context Learning for Zero-Shot Spoken Language Understanding
saa2e5088fa.description: arXiv:2611.28929v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Adapting spoken language understanding (SLU) systems to novel or revised label taxonomies conventionally requires additional labeled data and retraining, creating a bottleneck for real world deployment. While in-context learning with few-shot demonstrations offers an alternative, multi-modal generalization and scaling has been challenging. In this work, we investigate whether natural-language definitions alone can guide zero-shot SLU without demonstration exemplars, finding that symbolic definitions serve as the primary supervisory driver for adapting speech-text models. We operationalize this principle as Definition-Guided In-Context Learning (DG-ICL), a fine-tuning framework that decouples semantic categories from fixed lexical names. By
saa2e5088fa.summary: Researchers show natural-language label definitions alone can guide zero-shot spoken language understanding without demonstration examples.
saa2e5088fa.why: Suggests taxonomy changes in voice systems might be handled by updating definitions rather than collecting labeled data and retraining.

sde695f61a0.title: When Rubrics Do Not Decide: Silent Value Completion in LLM Evaluation
sde695f61a0.description: arXiv:2611.28940v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-criterion LLM judges often evaluate responses without specifying how conflicting criteria resolve, leaving the winner undetermined even under exact criterion scores. Issuing a strict verdict without declaring the required trade-off premise constitutes silent value completion. We introduce TradeoffBench to isolate this failure by separating rule execution from response scoring. On authoritative criterion vectors, six open-weight non-reasoning judges pass all dominance and equality controls yet pick unsupported winners on 9%-81% of 1,345 conflicts. All 577 order-stable choices follow an explicitly banned majority rule. Reasoning-enabled configurations drop anonymous-vector violations to 2 in 9,720 judgments under an explicit rule, yet c
sde695f61a0.summary: TradeoffBench is introduced to show multi-criterion LLM judges often pick winners on conflicting criteria without declaring the trade-off rule, with error rates from 9% to 81%.
sde695f61a0.why: Warns that LLM-as-judge evaluations can silently make unstated trade-off decisions, affecting the reliability of automated evaluation pipelines.

s10785db4cf.title: Micro Operational Robustness of LLMs on Code Generation
s10785db4cf.description: arXiv:2611.28957v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: It is now common practice in software development for large language models (LLMs) to be used to generate program code. It is desirable to evaluate the robustness of LLMs for this usage. This paper is concerned in particular with how sensitive LLMs are to variations in descriptions of the coding tasks. However, existing techniques for evaluating this robustness are unsuitable for code generation because the input data space of natural language (NL) descriptions is discrete and sparse. To address this problem, we propose a robustness evaluation method called scenario domain analysis, which aims to find the expected minimal change in the NL descriptions of coding tasks that would cause the LLMs to produce incorrect outputs. We have formally p
s10785db4cf.summary: An arXiv paper proposes a robustness evaluation method for how sensitive LLMs are to variations in natural-language descriptions of coding tasks.
s10785db4cf.why: Shows code-generation output can shift with small wording changes in task descriptions, which matters for relying on LLMs in development workflows.

sd95b3c0e0a.title: Learning Land-Surface Hydrology World Model from Satellite Observations
sd95b3c0e0a.description: arXiv:2611.28963v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A world model should tell us not only what will happen, but what would happen under a different action. Learned Earth models now forecast remarkably well, yet forecast skill says little about what their state means or how it responds to a changed driver. We build LandWM, a world model of land-surface water in which rain is the action, learned from seven years of SMAP and CYGNSS observations: physical observation operators tie its latent state to soil water, and a mass-conserving balance governs how that state responds to rain. Over the U.S. Southern Great Plains, the model, never shown a soil-moisture value, tracks 28 in-situ probes as well as the operational SMAP Level-4 product, even from CYGNSS alone, and a storm added to the forcing of
sd95b3c0e0a.summary: Researchers built LandWM, a land-surface water world model trained on seven years of SMAP and CYGNSS satellite observations, where rain is the action.

se1ca59684c.title: MolReJev: Decision Models Are In-Context Molecular Predictors
se1ca59684c.description: arXiv:2611.28965v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Molecular prediction helps prioritize compounds for screening. Specialized predictors are trained for a fixed set of tasks, limiting cross-task generalization. Language models can condition on task descriptions and have recently shown promise in molecular prediction. However, generating answers token by token adds inference cost, and general-purpose models often lack task-specific molecular knowledge. We thus propose MolReJev, which combines Jev-style candidate scoring with in-context learning (ICL) on a language model. MolReJev retrieves similar labeled examples from existing task data and scores candidate labels jointly in one forward pass. ICL improves predictions from the released general-purpose Kev checkpoint and the separately traine
se1ca59684c.summary: MolReJev is a proposed method that combines Jev-style candidate scoring with in-context learning on a language model for molecular prediction.
se1ca59684c.why: Offers a way to get task-general molecular predictions from a language model without per-task training, though the summary gives limited detail on results.

s3df20780fb.title: Who Gets Re-ranked When a Clinical Model Gains New Data?
s3df20780fb.description: arXiv:2611.28968v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hospitals often update a deployed risk model by adding a data source, such as laboratory results, that only some patients have. Work on safe model updates assumes fixed inputs and so ignores patients who lack the new data. The update has no new measurements for them, yet their rank can change, and a sick patient not yet tested can drop off an alert list. We split rank-based compatibility by data availability and pair it with error correction and alert-list effects. We compared each update with ordinary retraining on the old inputs, predicting ICU admission or death and hospital admission, on 78,475 emergency department visits from MC-MED and, in a pre-registered replication, 100,000 stays from MIMIC-IV-ED at a second hospital. Radiograph re
s3df20780fb.summary: A paper studies how adding a new data source, such as lab results available for only some patients, can reorder patient risk rankings in a deployed clinical model.
s3df20780fb.why: Highlights that safe model updates with partially available inputs can change alert lists for patients who lack the new data, a risk for deployed systems.

s20deb7627a.title: A Design Space for Data Agents: Insights from KDD Cup 2026
s20deb7627a.description: arXiv:2611.28970v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Data agents interpret analytical requests, gather evidence from heterogeneous sources, and compute results within finite resource budgets. We analyze the final code submissions of the ten highest-ranked teams in the KDD Cup 2026 Data Agents for Complex Data Analysis competition. We organize the observed design choices into three interacting layers, covering workflow orchestration, analytical functions, and working state. The comparison reveals recurring patterns for allocating computation in response to task progress, structuring evidence for computation and assessment, and preserving reusable artifacts with their provenance. Candidates that rely on the same evidence can inherit the same error, so interpreting their agreement requires traci
s20deb7627a.summary: An arXiv analysis of the final code submissions from the ten top KDD Cup 2026 teams identifies design patterns for data agents across three layers.
s20deb7627a.why: Gives engineers concrete architecture patterns for orchestrating data agents under compute budgets, drawn from competition-winning systems.

s7566f19924.title: World Models for Ocean Engineering: A Critical Review of Maritime Autonomy, Adaptive Latent Prediction, Digital Twins, and Biodiversity Monitoring
s7566f19924.description: arXiv:2611.28978v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Marine robots face partial observability, non-stationary dynamics, and sparse communication, motivating WMs that learn compact predictive states for planning. This review develops a functional taxonomy of WMs for ocean engineering, focusing on Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) and AdaJEPA's test-time adaptation within model predictive control, mapping them to navigation, adaptive sampling, digital twins, and biodiversity monitoring, and separating demonstrated evidence from prospective applications. The synthesis identifies key Gaps: benchmarks, uncertainty calibration, safe adaptation and proposes a research agenda for physics-informed, deployment-adaptive marine WMs validated through simulation and field missions.
s7566f19924.summary: A review surveys world models for ocean engineering, covering JEPA-based approaches, AdaJEPA test-time adaptation, digital twins, and biodiversity monitoring.

s1f2aa2a52a.title: CLASP: Complementary Layer Selection and Profiling for Zero-Shot OOD Detection using Vision-Language Models
s1f2aa2a52a.description: arXiv:2611.28986v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) enable zero-shot out-of-distribution (OOD) detection in medical imaging, yet existing approaches often rely on final-layer confidence or entropy-based layer selection, potentially missing complementary information. We show that low in-distribution (ID) confidence entropy does not reliably predict OOD discrimination. We introduce CLASP (Complementary Layer Selection and Profiling), an ID-only framework that jointly models layer--prompt responses and visual features. CLASP ranks visual encoder layers using Gaussian conditional mutual information and selects a compact subset through anchored spectral selection, without fixing the number of layers. It then combines the selected layer--prompt profiles with PCA-compr
s1f2aa2a52a.summary: CLASP is a proposed ID-only framework that selects and profiles vision-encoder layers to improve zero-shot out-of-distribution detection in medical imaging with VLMs.
s1f2aa2a52a.why: Suggests intermediate layers, not just final-layer confidence, can improve OOD detection in vision-language models used for medical imaging.

sde69d04cf8.title: Demystifying Classifier-Free Guidance for Auto-Regressive Image Generation
sde69d04cf8.description: arXiv:2611.29002v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Classifier-free guidance (CFG) has been widely adopted in autoregressive (AR) models for high-quality image generation. Despite its strong empirical performance, its mechanism in AR models remains unclear. This paper demystifies the mechanism of CFG through both empirical and theoretical studies. By examining the top-ranked semantics of different components in CFG, we show that texture information is primarily encoded in the difference between the conditional and unconditional logits, whereas both logits share previous-token repetition as their leading semantics. This strong repetition semantics obscures the desired texture information, causing greedy decoding from the conditional logits alone to produce nearly pure-color images. Through a
sde69d04cf8.summary: A paper examines how classifier-free guidance works in autoregressive image generation, finding texture information is encoded mainly in the difference between conditional and unconditional logits.
sde69d04cf8.why: Clarifies the mechanism behind CFG in autoregressive image models, which can inform tuning of guidance in generation pipelines.

s6fcbacc428.title: DoC: Learning to Defer or Commit for Timely, Accurate, and Stable Conversational Diagnosis Prediction
s6fcbacc428.description: arXiv:2611.29003v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Conversational diagnosis prediction requires accurate, early, and stable predictions from ongoing clinical dialogue, yet dialogue-level labels do not specify when to commit. We propose a two-phase framework for learning deferral and diagnosis decisions. First, iterative commitment-boundary estimation constructs Defer/diagnosis supervision without annotated commitment times. Second, Defer-aware supervised fine-tuning initializes a policy, refined through reinforcement learning with trajectory-level rewards for timeliness, first-commit accuracy, and post-commit stability. On EMSDialog and MediTOD, DoC commits early, achieving the highest first-commit accuracy among post-trained methods (76.7%/51.2%) and the lowest post-commit error overall (1
s6fcbacc428.summary: DoC is a two-phase framework that trains models to decide when to defer or commit to a diagnosis during conversational clinical dialogue, using reinforcement learning.

sa35c91a123.title: Consumer-Time Validity in Stateful AI Runtimes: Verifying Recovered State and Deferred Authority
sa35c91a123.description: arXiv:2611.29004v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stateful LLM serving engines and agent runtimes reuse execution state and deferred permissions across components and sessions. A cancellation, rollback, or approval is recorded by one component and relied on by another, and recording it does not make the later use valid: a downstream consumer may read state or dispatch an action whose identity, production status, allocation, or target revision has since changed. We call the missing check consumer-time validity and separate two forms. State validity governs what a consumer reads. On vLLM with LMCache, an interrupted KV load leaves unwritten blocks indexed, and a host-only counter rewind desynchronizes the GPU position, so a second tenant generates a schema-valid tool call naming the wrong te
sa35c91a123.summary: A paper introduces consumer-time validity, a check that verifies recovered state and deferred permissions are still valid when used by downstream components in stateful LLM serving and agent runtimes.
sa35c91a123.why: Identifies a correctness gap where cancellations or approvals recorded by one component may be stale when another acts on them, relevant to agent runtime design.

sa0ea29b2ff.title: NoHairCache: Calibrate-Once KV Cache Eviction with One Power-Law Exponent
sa0ea29b2ff.description: arXiv:2611.29006v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The decay exponent $\alpha$ in KV-cache eviction is an intrinsic property of the model: calibrated once on a single corpus, it transfers directly across domains. Attention-based accumulation (H2O) and recency-based sliding windows (StreamingLLM) are two dominant eviction frameworks, often treated as unrelated, but we show that they are the two endpoints of a single power-law family: by scoring each token as $s_i = A_i \cdot (t-i)^{-\alpha}$, where $A_i$ is cumulative attention and $\alpha$ controls the age penalty, H2O and StreamingLLM correspond to $\alpha=0$ and $\alpha\to\infty$, respectively (with StreamingLLM additionally hard-coding an attention-sink patch). The no-hair mechanism of \citet{xiang2026nohair} bounds the admissible range
sa0ea29b2ff.summary: NoHairCache proposes a KV-cache eviction method using a single power-law exponent that unifies H2O and StreamingLLM as endpoints and is calibrated once per model.
sa0ea29b2ff.why: Offers a single calibrated parameter for KV-cache eviction that claims to transfer across domains, relevant to inference memory optimization.

s0a90c99471.title: Mind the Trap As LLMs Guess the Data Model: Grain-Aware Guards Against Fan-out in Text-to-SQL and Its Benchmarks
s0a90c99471.description: arXiv:2611.29009v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Text-to-SQL systems built on large language models (LLMs) often aggregate over one-to-many and many-to-many joins, a classic trap: when the joined rows repeat an entity, a SUM or COUNT counts it more than once, yet the query runs and returns a plausible number. We characterize these fan-out errors by one condition on the relation an aggregate reads, which depends on two facts a schema does not show: each measure's grain, and how many rows a join on each key repeats. An audit that tests the condition on the data finds distorted gold answers for 4.2% of the dev questions of BIRD, a widely used benchmark, and BIRD's later, independent revision changed 44% of the answers the audit flags as definite fan-out, against 16% of unflagged ones. We rel
s0a90c99471.summary: A paper addresses fan-out errors in LLM-generated text-to-SQL, where aggregates over one-to-many joins double-count rows, and proposes grain-aware guards and audited benchmarks.
s0a90c99471.why: Silent double-counting in aggregates produces plausible wrong numbers, a real risk for LLM-driven analytics and BI query generation.

s93e7a0d01b.title: Watermark Claims Under Test: Lessons from Auditing a Production LLM
s93e7a0d01b.description: arXiv:2611.29018v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Can we tell whether an LLM is watermarked without knowing its secret key? Published black-box tests suggest that carefully designed prompts can reveal the statistical footprint of a watermark. This paper examines what happens when those tests move from controlled reference implementations to a deployed model whose watermarking parameters are undisclosed. We present an audit of the Red-Green watermark presence test on Claude. Across ten initial configurations, the published test never rejects on a model the provider states is watermarked, despite detecting a local reference at comparable sample sizes. Controlled experiments expose a failure mode: including the prompt in the watermark's repeated-context history suppresses marking exactly wher
s93e7a0d01b.summary: An audit of the Red-Green watermark presence test on Claude found the published test never rejected on a model the provider states is watermarked, across ten configurations.
s93e7a0d01b.why: Shows black-box watermark detection tests may fail on deployed models, relevant to anyone relying on provenance claims for LLM outputs.

sdce071d658.title: Irreducible Governance Structure for Autonomous Agent Systems: Fair Allocation, Strategy-Proofness, and Multi-Scale Composition
sdce071d658.description: arXiv:2611.31284v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous agent governance is commonly framed as a problem of enforcing correct execution. However, in multi-agent systems, an equally fundamental question precedes execution: which agents are allowed to act. In this paper, we show that allocation is not an auxiliary concern but a structural component of governance. When multiple agents compete for execution under constrained resources, any allocation mechanism introduces unavoidable trade-offs between fairness, efficiency, and resistance to strategic manipulation. We formalize this through a set of impossibility results, including Sybil amplification and the incompatibility of desirable allocation properties. We then show that these allocation constraints cannot be resolved within a single
sdce071d658.summary: An arXiv paper argues that deciding which agents may act is a structural part of multi-agent governance, formalizing fairness, efficiency, and strategy-proofness trade-offs.
sdce071d658.why: Offers formal allocation trade-offs for designing resource-constrained multi-agent systems, though it is a theoretical preprint.

sb02e0bf3ed.title: MOZAIC: An Audio-Video Deepfake Benchmark for Telling What Is Fake
sb02e0bf3ed.description: arXiv:2611.31301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Audio-video (AV) deepfakes can fake the face, the voice, or both. Most benchmarks only ask whether a clip is real or fake, so they cannot show whether a detector relies on the picture, the voice, or encoding traces. We present MOZAIC, a paired benchmark with a 4-way label in which every source clip is released in all four combinations of real or fake video and real or fake audio so each modality contribution can be measured directly. Fakes cover inner-face swapping, whole-frame video diffusion and voice conversion. MOZAIC has 137,745 clips from 15,014 source pairs and four tasks: T1 AV authenticity, T2 manipulation type, T3 identity verification and T4 explanation. We evaluate 12 AV multimodal LLMs (MLLMs), train four detectors and fine-tune
sb02e0bf3ed.summary: MOZAIC is a paired audio-video deepfake benchmark with 137,745 clips, labeling real or fake video and audio separately.
sb02e0bf3ed.why: Lets teams test whether deepfake detectors rely on video, audio, or encoding artifacts, improving evaluation beyond binary real-or-fake labels.

s9b5199cc4b.title: Conservative Overlap Fuzzy Rough Sets for Incomplete Data
s9b5199cc4b.description: arXiv:2611.31329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Attribute reduction in incomplete information systems is difficult because missing values break the equivalence-class structure of rough set theory. We propose the Conservative Overlap Fuzzy Rough Set (COFRS) model. Each object is described by its set of present attributes. The similarity of two objects is a weighted overlap on the attributes present in both, divided by the fixed number of attributes |A| instead of the size of their union, so missing values are penalised globally and are not matched as wildcards. From this similarity we define a soft dependency degree based on weighted granule consistency, and we search for reducts by greedy backward elimination in O(|U|^2 |A|^2) time. We show that the relation is symmetric and non-reflexive,
s9b5199cc4b.summary: Researchers propose the Conservative Overlap Fuzzy Rough Set model for attribute reduction in datasets with missing values.

sbc1d896f25.title: Beyond Static Charts: Benchmarking Interactive Chart-to-Code Generation for MLLMs
sbc1d896f25.description: arXiv:2611.31345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In recent years, multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have achieved significant progress in chart-to-code generation. However, existing benchmarks mainly focus on static charts, overlooking interactive charts that enable richer and more expressive data exploration. Unlike static chart-to-code generation, which emphasizes visual consistency, interactive chart-to-code evaluation targets behavioral consistency, requiring chart states to evolve correctly under sequences of user interactions, thereby rendering traditional one-step evaluation paradigms ineffective. To address this gap, we introduce ChartInt, the first benchmark specifically designed for interactive chart-to-code generation. ChartInt consists of 2,779 carefully annotated example
sbc1d896f25.summary: Researchers introduce a benchmark for interactive chart-to-code generation by multimodal LLMs, evaluating behavior across user interaction sequences.
sbc1d896f25.why: Shows that static chart benchmarks miss interactive behavior, so teams evaluating chart-generating models need richer tests.

s9a43d7dd6f.title: What People Choose Not to Say: A Multimodal Benchmark for Fine-Grained Information Manipulation in Conversations
s9a43d7dd6f.description: arXiv:2611.31346v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in MLLMs have improved social understanding, enabling models to recognize emotions and distinguish truthful from deceptive behaviors. However, existing benchmarks largely focus on coarse-grained emotion recognition or binary truth-deception detection, overlooking the diverse ways people manipulate information in conversations, such as withholding, leakage, fabrication, evasion, and defensive counterclaim. Understanding these behaviors requires reasoning about underlying facts, participant knowledge, and conversational context, making them difficult to evaluate reliably. To address this gap, we introduce InfoCon, a multimodal benchmark for fine-grained information manipulation in conversations. InfoCon identifies six fine-grain
s9a43d7dd6f.summary: Researchers released a multimodal benchmark testing how MLLMs detect fine-grained information manipulation such as withholding, leakage, and evasion in conversations.
s9a43d7dd6f.why: Points to gaps in current models' ability to reason about deception beyond simple truth-or-lie detection.

s1e984615ee.title: Antares-Smaug: Adversarial Names, Tokens and Attack Rewrites: Sanitisers Miss Unseen Generalisations
s1e984615ee.description: arXiv:2611.31347v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Laya is an open decision model: given a text, a question and K named options with descriptions, it returns one probability per option in a single pass, and software may act on the answer unseen. We attack six Laya models with 81 programmatic edits of 566 synthetic items (injected sentences, label leaks, edited descriptions, decoy options, invisible and look-alike characters, floods) and report the share of correctly answered items hijacked or lost, with bootstrap intervals. Attack wordings that no defence was built from win the attacker's option on 59% of items for released Laya and 36% for fine-tune v1 (trained on 109 written injections). An injection works through the option name: a sentence naming an option steers the released model even w
s1e984615ee.summary: Researchers attacked six Laya decision models with 81 programmatic edits and found that sanitizers miss unseen attack generalizations.
s1e984615ee.why: Shows that defenses built on known attacks may fail against novel prompt-injection wording, a risk for automated decision pipelines.

s6d2a8f9c18.title: ContextLure: Exploiting Benign Conversation History for Indirect Prompt Injection
s6d2a8f9c18.description: arXiv:2611.31424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As LLMs become more capable, agents can perform more complex tasks with tools and maintain longer interactions with users. These benign conversations contain evidence on task results, user concerns, and operational constraints. The risk is that attackers who can observe benign conversations (evidence) may construct stronger indirect prompt injections without increasing the attackers' control over prior turns or the later injection. However, we still lack a clear study of how effectively attackers can select and use this evidence. To address this gap, we introduce ContextLure, a red-teaming framework in which an attacker silently observes an existing benign conversation, extracts evidence, and constructs an injection. The challenges are twofol
s6d2a8f9c18.summary: ContextLure is a study showing attackers can use observed benign conversation history to craft stronger indirect prompt injections against LLM agents.
s6d2a8f9c18.why: Agents that carry long conversation context may expose new injection paths even when attackers do not control earlier turns.

s842222505d.title: Learning What vs. Learning How: Decomposing Task and Interface Competence in Agentic Training
s842222505d.description: arXiv:2611.31427v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents operate through harnesses that define system prompts, action formats, feedback loops, and resource constraints. A model may possess the knowledge needed to solve a task yet fail to express that knowledge through a particular harness. This raises a basic question: when a policy fails under a given harness, is it missing task knowledge or the competence to operate the interface? We distinguish two components of agentic competence: task competence, the knowledge and reasoning needed to solve a task, and interface competence, the ability to act on that knowledge through a given harness. Across four reasoning and agentic benchmarks, we show that harness-conditioned training yields vastly different outcomes depending on how these interac
s842222505d.summary: A paper decomposes agent failures into missing task knowledge versus inability to operate the interface, distinguishing task competence from interface competence.
s842222505d.why: Helps teams diagnose whether agent failures stem from the model's knowledge or from harness design and action formats.

s9216299406.title: Taxi: Analyzing Agents at (Real) Scale
s9216299406.description: arXiv:2611.31457v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this technical report, we present Taxi -- a system for debugging, clustering, and monitoring agents at scale. Taxi scales to millions of steps efficiently. This is made possible by a combination of scalable analysis methods. Taxi relies primarily on clustering to generate a taxonomy over steps for a structured overview of the data, and provides full SQL access for engineers and automated agents to ask complex questions. Clustering and querying are best used together in a hybrid pipeline guided by a coding agent. Taxi also includes an experimental integration of Jev-style decision models: models that map state and bounded questions directly to typed, probabilistic decisions. They add low-cost semantic routing and evaluation where embeddings
s9216299406.summary: Taxi is a technical report describing a system for debugging, clustering, and monitoring agents at scale, with SQL access for analysis over millions of steps.
s9216299406.why: Offers a practical approach for analyzing large volumes of agent execution traces, useful for teams running agents in production.

sd97bcf0fef.title: SpatialCraft: Evolving Procedural Intelligence from Experience and Skills for Spatial Reasoning Agents
sd97bcf0fef.description: arXiv:2611.31475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spatial reasoning agents increasingly rely on external tools, such as 3D reconstruction, segmentation, and geometric computation, to answer questions that a multimodal large language model (MLLM) cannot resolve from pixels alone. Tool access, however, shifts the bottleneck to orchestration: the agent must decide which tools to call, in what order, and how to interpret their outputs, yet a stateless agent repeats the same mistakes across tasks. We ask whether a frozen tool-using agent can improve its orchestration from its own interaction history, without parameter updates. We present SpatialCraft, a self-evolving framework that maintains two forms of external knowledge: Experiences, condition-action tactics distilled by contrasting rollouts o
sd97bcf0fef.summary: Researchers propose a method letting a frozen tool-using spatial reasoning agent improve its tool orchestration from its own interaction history.
sd97bcf0fef.why: Shows how agents can learn better tool-call sequencing from past runs without retraining the underlying model.

sc810ea565a.title: Evaluating Frontier-Model Agent Skills with Open-Weight Models in a Science Gateway
sc810ea565a.description: arXiv:2611.31480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scientific analyses that span many jobs and computing sites depend on workflow management systems to run reliably, but writing a production workflow requires expertise in such a system, which many domain scientists do not have. Coding agents can supply this expertise when they are guided by skills and packaged procedures for recurring tasks. We wrote skills and specialist agents for the Pegasus workflow management system with a frontier model, and the PegasusAI Studio science gateway offers them to scientists through a chat interface. New users without frontier-model credits need an open-weight model, served at no cost on research cyberinfrastructure, but skills written for a frontier model may not work with an open-weight solution. This pape
sc810ea565a.summary: Researchers describe skills and specialist agents for the Pegasus workflow system, offered to scientists via the PegasusAI Studio science gateway chat interface.
sc810ea565a.why: Illustrates packaging frontier-model coding agent skills for domain users, with evaluation using open-weight models.

s08f8a7fd6a.title: XRL4T1D: A Post-hoc Explainability Framework for Reinforcement Learning in Type 1 Diabetes Management
s08f8a7fd6a.description: arXiv:2611.31498v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) requires lifelong insulin therapy, and reinforcement learning (RL) has shown promise for automated dosing in the UVA/Padova simulator. However, the decisions of RL controllers remain difficult to interpret. We present XRL4T1D, a post-hoc explainability framework for evaluating pretrained insulin-dosing policies without retraining. Each policy uses 60 minutes of continuous glucose monitor (CGM) and administered-insulin history, sampled every 5 minutes, to recommend insulin. We use SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to compare the importance of CGM and insulin-history inputs and summarize insulin-history attributions over three 20-minute windows motivated by insulin-on-board. s08f8a7fd6a.summary: Researchers present XRL4T1D, a post-hoc explainability framework using SHAP to evaluate pretrained reinforcement learning insulin-dosing policies without retraining.
s08f8a7fd6a.why: Offers a way to interpret RL controller decisions in a safety-critical medical setting without changing the trained policy.

s1d8eb48ffe.title: PatientFlowSynth: Evaluating FHIR Agents with Matched Patient Charts
s1d8eb48ffe.description: arXiv:2611.31521v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agents that search patient charts must classify claims from retrieved records, including cases with missing or conflicting evidence. PatientFlowSynth provides 18,000 tasks from 225 synthetic patients and 18 templates that hold the patient, question, and retrieval program fixed across chart variants representing four evidence states. Re-executing the program verifies each variant's reference answer, evidence sets, and search requirements. s1d8eb48ffe.summary: PatientFlowSynth is a benchmark of 18,000 tasks from 225 synthetic patients for evaluating FHIR chart-search agents on claims with missing or conflicting evidence.
s1d8eb48ffe.why: Gives teams a controlled benchmark for testing healthcare records agents on evidence states that affect answer correctness.

sd0679e7d06.title: One Step, Four Clocks: How GUI Agents Fall Out of Step
sd0679e7d06.description: arXiv:2611.31522v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: GUI agents can choose correct actions yet fail as interfaces change during deliberation. Latency alone cannot explain these failures because actions may become invalid at different interaction stages. We model four events: environment change, observation availability, decision commitment, and action receipt (EODA). We introduce ChronotopeGym to study these failures under Paused, Replay, and Live execution. Across five tasks, agents can fail in Live despite succeeding when responses remain valid, even when actions meet deadlines. On Moving Balloon, updating a pending click raises success from 0% to 100% without changing response time. sd0679e7d06.summary: Researchers model four timing events in GUI agent interactions and introduce ChronotopeGym, finding agents can fail in live execution despite succeeding under valid responses.
sd0679e7d06.why: Shows that latency and interface changes during deliberation can invalidate agent actions, a concern for deploying GUI automation.

s8642462bbe.title: Agent Evaluation Without Ground Truth: A Null Proportion Perspective
s8642462bbe.description: arXiv:2611.31539v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The correctness of actions taken by agents is typically evaluated against known, externally verified ground truth labels, such as whether a proof is correct or whether code compiles and passes unit tests. However, as coding and science agents are entrusted with more end-to-end autonomy -- proposing interventions, running experiments, and deciding what to deploy and investigate next -- whether an agent's actions genuinely improve an outcome must be inferred from noisy, often inconclusive experiments. To evaluate agents in this setting, we define agent quality as a weighted sum of correct decisions along its trajectory, using sequences of $e$-values as statistical evidence regarding correctness in place of ground-truth labels. Our framework acc
s8642462bbe.summary: Researchers propose a null-proportion framework for evaluating agents whose actions must be inferred from noisy, inconclusive experiments rather than ground-truth labels.
s8642462bbe.why: Addresses how to measure whether autonomous agents genuinely improve outcomes when no verified ground truth exists.

s45d0a75ba2.title: Agent Recovery Gone Wrong: Measuring Harm Beyond Duplicate Calls
s45d0a75ba2.description: arXiv:2611.31554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Code-executing LLM agents submit blocks of code that issue several API writes. If a block fails after some of its writes have taken effect, the agent rewrites the block and continues. It is unknown how often such a recovery harms the external state when the failure occurs naturally in the code written by the agent. In this paper, we measure it on recorded trajectories of AppWorld agents. In a stratified random sample of 200 candidate episodes across ten models, 145 are partial executions confirmed by the database state. In the sample, 30 of 143 confirmed partial executions with a determinable outcome are followed by a harmful recovery, and its violation remains at the end of the run, which gives a stratification-weighted estimate of 24.6%. Tw
s45d0a75ba2.summary: A study of AppWorld agent trajectories finds that recovering from partially executed code blocks can harm external state through repeated API writes.
s45d0a75ba2.why: Highlights that agent retry logic can cause unintended duplicate side effects in production API environments.

s4b55c71e9c.title: COGENT: A Modular Cognitive Architecture for Agentic User Simulation
s4b55c71e9c.description: arXiv:2611.31559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-based user simulation can support interface design, accessibility research, and interactive-agent evaluation, but standard computer-use agents are optimized for task completion rather than reproducing how people perceive, reason, and act. We introduce COGENT (COGnitive agENT), a modular cognitive architecture for simulating user interaction with desktop interfaces. COGENT draws on established cognitive theories, such as Norman's action cycle and ACT-R, to enable explainable, intervenable, and modular user simulation by decomposing the simulation process into cognitive modules with explicit representations of perception, memory, user state, intentions, and action selection. We begin by presenting six intervenability demonstrations, each tr
s4b55c71e9c.summary: Researchers introduce COGENT, a modular cognitive architecture that simulates user interaction with desktop interfaces based on cognitive theories.
s4b55c71e9c.why: Offers a more explainable approach to simulating users for interface design and accessibility testing, beyond task-completion agents.

s71e21bfe60.title: Off-the-Shelf Autonomous Agents for Game Playtesting
s71e21bfe60.description: arXiv:2611.31570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In playtesting games, a human operator is typically required to test most gameplay elements. In this work we present Buddy, an autonomous game solving agent which can solve long time horizon objectives in an unseen 3D role-playing game using off-the-shelf language model systems. Buddy will take actions, receive feedback on those actions, and pursue a goal across many turns. No written walkthrough or model training of any kind is required, and we show that this paradigm holds in a novel environment where the agent must discover solutions via exploration rather than recalling them from pretraining. We demonstrate three downstream capabilities: game solving with no provided walkthrough, logging bug tickets for encountered difficulties, and conve
s71e21bfe60.summary: Researchers present Buddy, an autonomous agent that plays an unseen 3D role-playing game using off-the-shelf language model systems without walkthroughs or training.
s71e21bfe60.why: Suggests general-purpose LLM systems can handle long-horizon exploration tasks like playtesting with no task-specific training.

se85d829d86.title: Safe Autoformalization: Sufficiency and Necessity with Entailment Graphs
se85d829d86.description: arXiv:2611.31571v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autoformalization translates a natural-language statement into a formula that captures its intent, which depends on the statement's context: the background that disambiguates it. LLMs make autoformalization practical, but their probabilistic output carries no formal guarantees. We propose techniques for safe autoformalization that certify one-sided logical adequacy: a formula sufficient for the intent is safe to enforce, and a formula necessary for it is safe to rely on. We use LLMs to generate candidate formulas and order them by logical strength in an Entailment Graph (EG), an ordering a solver decides. Each edge carries a residual and a co-residual, the two adjoints of the entailment order, all fixed by the candidate pool alone. In a conte
se85d829d86.summary: Researchers propose techniques for safe autoformalization that certify one-sided logical adequacy using LLM-generated candidate formulas ordered by logical strength.
se85d829d86.why: Offers a route to attach partial formal guarantees to LLM-generated logical specifications, though the text gives limited deployment detail.

s1c3033b758.title: Provably Near-Optimal PQ in the Extended Zador Model
s1c3033b758.description: arXiv:2611.31579v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates Product Quantization (PQ) Optimization with Gaussian data. It offers three key contributions (i) a proof that SVD is the optimal preconditioning rotation for PQ; (ii) a new Extended Zador (EZ) estimator of the $k$-means quantization cost that is accurate in low bit rates and low dimensions; and (iii) a novel segmentation algorithm based on 1-d bin packing of global bit allocations. The result is a simple algorithm (EZPQ) with strong approximation guarantees. It matches OPQ's empirical accuracy while providing a per-instance distortion lower bound certificate under the Gaussian EZ cost model. On typical real embedding spectra, EZPQ with 2 bits per coordinate is often certifiably within 1% of the optimum in this model. I
s1c3033b758.summary: Researchers prove SVD is the optimal preconditioning rotation for product quantization on Gaussian data and introduce an EZPQ algorithm with approximation guarantees.
s1c3033b758.why: Provides theoretical grounding and a simple algorithm for tuning vector compression, relevant to embedding search infrastructure.

seef28d1c21.title: Frequency-Conditioned Privacy Auditing of Fine-Tuned Language Models
seef28d1c21.description: arXiv:2611.31581v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are increasingly fine-tuned on sensitive data, where the same person's information may appear multiple times across records. This can cause models to memorize sensitive information, but memorization does not necessarily mean that the information can be recovered. A more serious privacy risk arises when the model begins to reproduce that information during generation. In this paper, we study how often sensitive information must appear in the fine-tuning data before it becomes recoverable. Across four language models, we vary the frequency of email addresses and phone numbers from $1\times$ to $50\times$ and compare standard fine-tuning, gradient clipping, and differentially private training. We find that the number of rep
seef28d1c21.summary: Researchers study how often sensitive information must appear in fine-tuning data before a language model can reproduce it during generation, across four models.
seef28d1c21.why: Informs privacy risk assessment for fine-tuning on records where the same person's data appears multiple times.

s4d3997d08c.title: Monitorable-by-design architectures for a post-Astra world: a compartmentalization-based approach
s4d3997d08c.description: arXiv:2611.31610v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Frontier models like GPT-6 Astra are increasingly able to do substantial reasoning without a monitorable chain of thought, chains of thought are becoming less legible, and are often monitored asynchronously to reduce cost. With the future of chain of thought monitoring unclear, it may be necessary to design LLMs with monitorability in mind. We propose a modification to existing LLM architectures based on GRAM, SGTM, DEMix, BTS, and similar methods to compartmentalize dangerous capabilities so that their use, especially in combination with dangerous reasoning types that may indicate strategic adversarial use, can be monitored more cheaply than chain of thought in a way that might outlast monitorable chain of thought. We propose several variant
s4d3997d08c.summary: Researchers propose modifying LLM architectures to compartmentalize dangerous capabilities so their use is easier to monitor when chain-of-thought becomes less legible.
s4d3997d08c.why: Points to architecture-level design choices for maintaining oversight of frontier models as reasoning becomes harder to monitor.

se5fa006d6d.title: Multi-agent System for Automatic Discovery of Pareto-optimal Meta-solvers for PDEs
se5fa006d6d.description: arXiv:2611.31611v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Designing linear solvers for discretized partial differential equations requires problem-specific expertise. We present a multi-agent framework, in which language-model agents propose, critique, implement, and evaluate solver configurations assembled from Krylov methods, preconditioners, block factorizations, and neural operators. Inside the proposing agent, a non-dominated sorting genetic evolutionary algorithm evolves the population of meta-solvers toward the Pareto front of six measured quantities, so that one run returns a front of trade-offs rather than a single tuned solver. The system runs on small open-weight language models served on a single laptop, and we compare it with a single agent on four problems. For three-dimensional acoust
se5fa006d6d.summary: A multi-agent framework uses language-model agents and a genetic algorithm to evolve Pareto-optimal linear solver configurations for discretized PDEs.
se5fa006d6d.why: Shows agent-driven search can automate solver design across trade-off metrics, though the text gives limited detail on results.

sfb383e81ff.title: Self-Improving Long-Horizon Reasoning by Learning Summaries from Local Continuations
sfb383e81ff.description: arXiv:2611.31621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reasoning models degrade as their context grows, so longer reasoning traces do not by themselves give longer effective horizons. One way to extend the horizon is to compress the reasoning history into a compact state from time to time and continue from the state. Existing methods train the state with the final-answer reward or distill it from a stronger model. Neither signal is tailored to measure the contribution of the state alone. We observe that a reasoning model that degrades over long trajectories still behaves reliably in short contexts. We aim to preserve this short-context behavior when compressing the reasoning history. Motivated by this, we train a separate summarizer with Delta-KL, a reward computed from the frozen reasoning model
sfb383e81ff.summary: Researchers propose training reasoning models to compress their reasoning history into summaries by measuring the state's contribution through local continuations.
sfb383e81ff.why: Targets degradation of reasoning models over long contexts, a practical limit for long-horizon agent tasks.

s60604a1190.title: Wavefront: Low-Rank Drafting with Parallel Causal Refinement for Speculative Decoding
s60604a1190.description: arXiv:2611.31638v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates LLM inference by letting a cheap drafter propose tokens that the target model verifies in parallel. Parallel block drafters such as DFlash and P-EAGLE propose a whole block in one forward pass, but they lose the dependence between tokens in the block; DSpark restores part of it with a lightweight correction head that runs sequentially. Measuring DSpark, we find that this head overrides the base prediction on most slots, so the expensive base readout through the target's full lm_head mostly provides a seed. We therefore propose Wavefront, which follows a simple principle: shrink the base and strengthen the correction head. Wavefront replaces the full lm_head with a learned low-rank base, conditions the correcti
s60604a1190.summary: Researchers propose Wavefront, a speculative decoding method that uses low-rank drafting with parallel causal refinement to speed LLM inference.
s60604a1190.why: Faster verified token drafting can cut LLM serving latency and compute costs for engineers running inference.

s600513770b.title: E2SIM: Long-Horizon Simulation of Everyday Human Behavior with Evolving States
s600513770b.description: arXiv:2611.31641v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents are increasingly expected to support users over long periods, across work, and daily life. This requires modeling not only who users are, but also how their goals, interests, activities, and interactions evolve over time. A challenge in longitudinal user simulation is maintaining consistency between these evolving states and the consequences of actions in a shared environment. We introduce E2SIM, a longitudinal user simulation framework that jointly models evolving actor states and a dynamic shared environment. E2SIM connects actor-state updates with shared-world changes through a feedback loop linking immediate actions, delayed outcomes, and actor-specific observations across work and life. This allows the consequences of earlier a
s600513770b.summary: Researchers introduce E2SIM, a framework that simulates long-horizon everyday human behavior by jointly modeling evolving user states and a shared environment.
s600513770b.why: Consistent longitudinal user simulation could help teams test agents that support users over long periods.

sf4ea7faa42.title: Constructing physical mechanisms with artificial intelligence
sf4ea7faa42.description: arXiv:2611.31653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mechanisms recur across the sciences: the equation for heat in a solid also describes molecular diffusion or a Brownian particle. A mechanism is rarely written in one equation; its operation, boundaries, parameters and closures are stated at different steps of a derivation, where methods that read text or fit formulas miss it. We built an equation-native system that reads the equations of all 2.5 million arXiv manuscripts, and show that mechanisms can be compiled from them and constructed by deterministic calculation. A constructor detaches, transfers, unfolds, composes and joins their parts across disciplines; where parts do not fit, the failure is an equation for the missing term. Constructions turn a threshold reactor into a memory that a
sf4ea7faa42.summary: Researchers describe an equation-native AI system that reads 2.5 million arXiv manuscripts and compiles physical mechanisms from their equations.

sbaaee125a7.title: Stranded Compute in AI Inference Workloads: Recovering Value Through Demand Aggregation
sbaaee125a7.description: arXiv:2611.31654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI inference infrastructure is commonly analyzed as an energy business. Under full total cost accounting it is not: in the reference deployment modeled here, capital recovery is 87.3% of fully loaded cost per token and electricity 3.7%. Because capital accrues per unit time irrespective of use, accelerator value is destroyed by non-utilization rather than by consumption. Yet, SLO qualified goodput reaches only 59.6% of nameplate throughput, and the decomposition of the loss chain shows that 25.2 of the 40.4 lost percentage points arise from scheduling idleness and stranded burst reserve. Both are properties of a tenant's demand portfolio rather than of its silicon, and neither is diversifiable by a single tenant acting alone. Modelling reserv
sbaaee125a7.summary: A paper argues AI inference economics are dominated by capital recovery and idle accelerator time, and that demand aggregation could recover stranded compute value.
sbaaee125a7.why: Low utilization of accelerators drives inference cost per token, so scheduling and demand aggregation matter for infrastructure planning.

sf629944ee2.title: Look Before You Commit: Visual-Evidence-Guided Decoding for Multimodal Diffusion Language Models
sf629944ee2.description: arXiv:2611.31677v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Diffusion multimodal large language models rely on confidence to decide when to commit candidate tokens during generation. In multimodal tasks, however, confidence cannot distinguish whether a candidate originates from image evidence or the language prior. We perform paired forward ablation and find that nearly nine out of ten high-confidence commits are insensitive to the image, while degenerate and hallucination samples exhibit significant increases in the entropy of deep-layer attention organization. Based on this diagnosis, we propose CD-APC, a training-free decoding method. CD-APC performs evidence-adjusted scoring within a base-supported pool and uses dual gating based on model acceptability and contrastive concentration to decide wheth
sf629944ee2.summary: Researchers propose CD-APC, a visual-evidence-guided decoding method for diffusion multimodal LLMs that reduces image-insensitive token commits and hallucinations.
sf629944ee2.why: Grounding decoding in image evidence targets hallucination in multimodal models that teams deploy on vision tasks.

sfa789566d2.title: LimoBench: How Street Smart Are Large Language Models?
sfa789566d2.description: arXiv:2611.31682v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have transformed how humans interact with information, enabling natural-language interfaces across various domains. They are increasingly deployed for geospatial applications including map-based question answering, location-based services, and natural-language interfaces to spatial databases. But are LLMs truly location-aware, able to reliably interpret and precisely answer location queries involving real-world coordinates, points of interest (POIs), and geospatial distances? To answer this concretely, we present LimoBench, a street-level benchmark of 82 natural-language location queries over seven canonical spatial operations: geocoding, reverse geocoding, routing, directionality, range search, $k$-nearest-neighb
sfa789566d2.summary: Researchers present LimoBench, a benchmark testing whether large language models reliably answer location queries involving coordinates, POIs and geospatial distances.
sfa789566d2.why: Shows gaps in LLM geospatial reliability, relevant to teams building map or location-based natural-language interfaces.

s88b4fee001.title: CROSS-Calib: Selective Channel Calibration for Ultrasound Reconstruction
s88b4fee001.description: arXiv:2611.31684v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ultrasound imaging provides views of internal tissue in real time for medical diagnosis. However, ultrasound signals may be affected by interference, and correcting errors and removing transient interference while preserving valid echoes remains challenging. We propose CROSS-Calib, a channel recovery method that uses predictions from other channels as references for amplitude and phase calibration, while a gate using context selectively combines calibrated measurements with predicted echoes to retain usable samples and repair unreliable ones. On the in vivo test set, CROSS-Calib outperforms all baseline models under gain errors and transient interference, while phantom tests show that the model restores cyst contrast with echo widths of wire
s88b4fee001.summary: Researchers propose CROSS-Calib, a channel recovery method that calibrates ultrasound signals using predictions from other channels and a context-based gate.

s942a72dbf7.title: PRETZEL: A Benchmark for Cyclic Peptide Structure Prediction
s942a72dbf7.description: arXiv:2611.31708v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Macrocyclic peptides are a growing therapeutic modality, and co-folding models are increasingly used to predict their structures.
