Yet published evaluations rely on small, loosely curated target sets that differ from paper to paper, so results are not comparable, and most report pose RMSD alone, without checking whether the predicted molecule is chemically correct. We introduce PRETZEL (Prediction of Ring-Enclosed Topology: Zero-shot Evaluation of cycLic peptides), a benchmark of 285 curated cyclic peptide-protein complexes spanning three cyclization chemistries, all post-dating the training cutoff of every model evaluated. PRETZEL has three components: PRETZEL-SET, an evaluation set annotated by cyclization chemistry and chemical novelty; PRE
s942a72dbf7.summary: Researchers introduce PRETZEL, a benchmark of 285 curated cyclic peptide-protein complexes for evaluating structure prediction, including chemical correctness checks.
s942a72dbf7.why: Standardized benchmarks make co-folding model results comparable and check chemical validity beyond pose RMSD.

s0ea9aa954b.title: Reproducing History Is Not Enough: Intervention-Level Assurance for LLM-Generated Simulators
s0ea9aa954b.description: arXiv:2611.31736v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models can now write simulation programs of operational processes and workflows. These programs can be reused to answer what-if questions on new records and policies. However, a program that reproduces recorded history can still give wrong answers to what-if questions; requested changes may be applied wrongly, or they may be applied to records other than the ones the question is about, or the program may stop being valid once its policy is revised. Current checks return a pass-or-fail verdict for the whole program, which says little about whether any single answer can be trusted. We propose Vouch, a library that judges whether an answer from a generated simulator can be trusted for the change being asked about. Each what-if que
s0ea9aa954b.summary: Researchers argue that LLM-generated simulators passing historical reproduction checks can still fail what-if questions, and propose intervention-level assurance.
s0ea9aa954b.why: Whole-program pass/fail checks can miss wrong what-if behavior, a risk for teams using generated simulation code for policy decisions.

sb663e004c7.title: GreenDynaMix: Thermal-Aware Dynamic Mixed-Precision MoE LLM Inference Systems
sb663e004c7.description: arXiv:2611.31737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sustained Large Language Model (LLM) inference generates significant heat that exacerbates silicon aging and reduces GPU reliability. Because GPU temperature fluctuates continuously with workload intensity and ambient conditions, keeping it in a safe range requires real-time frequency scaling, which inevitably comes at the cost of either throughput or accuracy. To address this tightly coupled challenge, we propose GreenDynaMix, the first runtime system to jointly integrate a DVFS-based thermal manager with a dynamic precision-tuning throughput compensator. A sensitivity-aware allocator leverages intrinsic importance signals from the Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) router to assign higher precision to critical experts, preserving accuracy. Experiment
sb663e004c7.summary: Researchers present GreenDynaMix, a runtime system combining DVFS-based thermal management with dynamic mixed-precision tuning for MoE LLM inference.
sb663e004c7.why: Thermal-aware scaling addresses GPU reliability and throughput trade-offs during sustained inference workloads.

s160e3afedf.title: FN-Prune: Training-Free Expert Pruning with Finite RMSNorm Perturbations
s160e3afedf.description: arXiv:2611.31747v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Expert pruning reduces the memory footprint of mixture-of-experts language models, but retaining model quality depends on which experts are removed. Frequency- and magnitude-based scores measure the expert in isolation and overlook how normalization consumes its contribution: subtracting one expert changes both the direction of the residual stream and the scale applied to what remains. We propose FN-Prune, a training-free criterion that compares the next RMSNorm outputs before and after subtracting each router-weighted expert contribution, holding original routes and weights fixed. Squared differences are averaged over all calibration tokens in one pass; low-scoring experts are physically deleted at uniform per-layer ratios, and inference rer
s160e3afedf.summary: Researchers propose FN-Prune, a training-free expert pruning criterion for mixture-of-experts models that accounts for RMSNorm effects after removing an expert.
s160e3afedf.why: Training-free pruning could reduce MoE memory footprint while better preserving model quality for deployment.

s6eb51df2ae.title: TACT-Bench: Testing Adaptive Conversational Threats against Tool-Use Agents
s6eb51df2ae.description: arXiv:2611.31756v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The growing autonomy of AI agents in using external tools and making decisions has created an urgent need for comprehensive safety benchmarks. Existing benchmarks test compromised tool channels or adaptive multi-turn attacks, though they may not capture the unique capabilities of policy-governed tool-use agents, which must resist unauthorized requests without abandoning the legitimate work embedded in the same interaction. To fill this gap, we introduce TACT-Bench, a stateful benchmark built around scenario-specific stories, personas, manipulation tactics, and response-adaptive escalation. Each adversarial task targets an action explicitly prohibited by the policy provided to the assistant, while the policy remains hidden from the attacking u
s6eb51df2ae.summary: Researchers introduce TACT-Bench, a stateful benchmark testing whether policy-governed tool-use agents resist adaptive conversational threats while completing legitimate work.
s6eb51df2ae.why: Tool-using agents need tests for resisting unauthorized requests without abandoning legitimate tasks in the same interaction.

sfa3edd752f.title: Verified Proof Refactoring with Codex and Qwen
sfa3edd752f.description: arXiv:2611.31762v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We refactor existing Lean 4 proofs to reduce source length and checking cost while preserving theorem statements and compatibility across Lean versions. A locally served Qwen model uses the open-source Codex CLI to inspect source, retrieve declarations, and test proof replacements. The host keeps a replacement only if it improves the objective and Lean accepts it on every required version. A deterministic CPU pass then refines the verified proofs. On the 60 problems in Lean Refactor Arena, model search achieves a local mean combined score of 82.07, and cleanup raises it to 82.18. The final proofs pass all 127 required proof--version checks. Our system placed first in the open-source LLM track of Lean Refactor Arena at VeriCodeGen.
sfa3edd752f.summary: A workflow uses a locally served Qwen model with the Codex CLI to refactor Lean 4 proofs, keeping changes only when Lean accepts them across versions.
sfa3edd752f.why: Shows verified, automated code refactoring with local models, useful for teams maintaining formal proof codebases.

s7806e40164.title: SciFig2Data: A Workflow for Recovering Structured Data from Scientific Figures
s7806e40164.description: arXiv:2611.31787v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scientific measurements reported in scholarly articles are often embedded in compound figures rather than available as machine-readable data. Recovering these measurements at literature scale requires an integrated workflow for figure localization, panel decomposition, chart identification, numerical reconstruction, and experimental context association. We present \textit{SciFig2Data}, an automated, high-throughput workflow for harvesting structured experimental data from scientific PDF repositories. The system integrates multi-scale document element detection, adaptive compound figure decomposition, two-stage OCR-based semantic filtering, Swin-based chart classification, and instruction-guided multimodal large language model (MLLM) reconstru
s7806e40164.summary: Researchers present SciFig2Data, an automated workflow that recovers structured numerical data from charts in scientific PDF figures.
s7806e40164.why: Automated extraction of figure data could enable literature-scale datasets for research and data teams.

s8eb6158b71.title: AGL-SKILL: Coding Harnesses as Agentic Optimizers
s8eb6158b71.description: arXiv:2611.31794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Frontier models are increasingly used through harnesses as agents, with growing autonomy to do useful work. Agent performance can often be enhanced by the use of skills: reusable workflows, code, and prompts that provide task-related information or guide the behaviour of the model. Skills, being textual in nature, present themselves as another editable surface to be optimized; current methods have improved on handcrafting and one-shot generation by treating skill development as an iterative process, using score-driven search to tweak and improve performance. In this paper, we demonstrate the efficacy of the agents themselves as optimizers: across five benchmarks, a coding agent without guidance substantially improves every target and outperfo
s8eb6158b71.summary: Researchers present AGL-SKILL, which treats agent skills as editable text optimized iteratively with score-driven search inside coding harnesses.
s8eb6158b71.why: Optimizing agent skills as a search surface could improve agent performance without manual handcrafting.

s3ccf039f49.title: Constructive Causal Abstraction and a Case Study in Mechanistic Interpretability
s3ccf039f49.description: arXiv:2611.31795v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing frameworks in causal abstraction first propose a high-level causal model, and then verify whether its interventional effects agree with those of a given micro-level model - the two models are declared causally consistent when the discrepancy is zero. However, proposing a consistent macro causal model is difficult, because macro causal relations are almost never well-defined, since distinct micro-level interventions associated with the same apparent macro intervention can produce different effects. Our central insight is that causally consistent macro-level models can be obtained constructively: ill-defined macro interventions can be interpreted as missing variables on the macro level, and can be accounted for by introducing a complem
s3ccf039f49.summary: An arXiv paper proposes constructive causal abstraction, arguing macro causal models should be built to be consistent with micro-level models rather than verified after the fact, with an interpretability case study.
s3ccf039f49.why: Offers a method for building high-level causal explanations of neural networks, relevant to engineers doing mechanistic interpretability.

sf2d6acc853.title: A Generative AI Agent to Emulate Interactive Human-driven Vehicles for Automated Driving Testing in Urban Areas
sf2d6acc853.description: arXiv:2611.31797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Realistic modeling of human-driven vehicle (HDV) interactions is essential for automated driving safety testing in urban areas. Existing methods struggle to reproduce realistic safety-critical interactions involving high collision risk for the following reasons: they often assume full observability, overlooking interactions arising from occlusion. Driving styles are mainly characterized by vehicle maneuvers, limiting the diversity of safety-critical interaction behaviors. Moreover, learning signals from safety-critical interactions can be diluted by non-critical driving behaviors. To address these issues, we propose a generative AI agent to emulate interactive HDVs. The agent incorporates field-of-view modeling to account for driver visibilit
sf2d6acc853.summary: Researchers present a generative AI agent that emulates interactive human-driven vehicles to generate safety-critical urban interactions for testing automated driving systems.
sf2d6acc853.why: Provides a way to produce realistic, occlusion-aware test scenarios for validating autonomous driving software in urban settings.

sabfcc175f2.title: Compressible Representations: Functional Spines in Deep Neural Networks
sabfcc175f2.description: arXiv:2611.31817v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep networks embed inputs in high-dimensional representations, but how much of this capacity actually drives behavior? We introduce a framework for identifying, at each layer, the subspace of the representation that is functionally sensitive to the task. Using a matrix analogous to the Fisher information but defined over the hidden representation, we rank directions by their influence on downstream computation and project onto the most task-sensitive subspace. Across pretrained vision networks, representations are remarkably compressible: a small fraction of the task-sensitive subspace preserves most performance, often requiring far fewer dimensions than geometric alternatives. We find that this compressed representation is also more robust
sabfcc175f2.summary: A paper introduces a method using a Fisher-like matrix to find the task-sensitive subspace of each layer in deep networks, finding pretrained vision network representations are highly compressible.
sabfcc175f2.why: Suggests much of a network's representation capacity is unused by behavior, which could inform model compression and efficiency work.

s07b2aecd22.title: GaokaoMathGen: Chinese Gaokao Mathematics Finale Problem Generation Controlled by Latent Reasoning Structures
s07b2aecd22.description: arXiv:2611.31823v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generating Chinese Gaokao mathematics finale problems requires controlling not only the included skills, but also the underlying mathematical kernel and solution path. Existing LLM-based methods mainly rely on surface-level specifications, while the realized difficulty of generated problems cannot be determined directly from prompted targets. Therefore, we propose GaokaoMathGen, a framework for Chinese Gaokao mathematics finale problem generation controlled by latent reasoning structures. It extracts standardized latent reasoning structures from seed problems and performs constrained synthesis using skills, methods, a core identity, and a pivot step as structural controls. We further estimate realized difficulty through logical-quality filter
s07b2aecd22.summary: GaokaoMathGen is a framework that generates Chinese Gaokao math finale problems by controlling latent reasoning structures rather than surface prompt specifications.

s1c8a2e400c.title: Not All Interpretation Methods Are Created Equal: Tiered Evaluation of AI Interpretability
s1c8a2e400c.description: arXiv:2611.31833v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As AI transitions to sociotechnical deployments, uninterpretable models pose serious threats to reliability, public trust and contestability. However, not all interpretation methods are created equal: for interpretability to enhance deployment safety and effectiveness, interpretation methods must be evaluated in a tiered system to differentiate evidence levels of trustworthiness, rather than validated through isolated interpretation instances. Our core vision is that elevating the evaluation of interpretation methods to a core AI assessment metric will drive robust knowledge discovery from data (KDD) and ensure safe, contestable sociotechnical deployments of AI. To this end, we propose TRUST, a tiered evaluation framework that builds upon the
s1c8a2e400c.summary: A position paper argues interpretation methods should be evaluated in a tiered system that grades evidence of trustworthiness, rather than validated through isolated instances.
s1c8a2e400c.why: Suggests teams should judge interpretability tools by graded evidence levels before relying on them for deployment safety decisions.

s87097a0602.title: Modeling Event-Conditioned Emotional Expression Response with LLM Agents in a Synthetic Social Simulation
s87097a0602.description: arXiv:2611.31851v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Emotions are central drivers of human behavior, yet most behavioral models fail to capture their role in shaping perception, decision-making, and collective action. Application areas such as emergency response and public health are especially constrained by the lack of emotion-aware modeling. While large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into agent-based models (ABMs), little work has examined how to endow LLM agents with emotional reasoning or validated their ability to reproduce empirically observed emotional patterns. This study addresses this gap by introducing a hierarchical prompting framework that conditions LLM agents with demographic, psychological, and contextual cues to generate event-conditioned emotional response
s87097a0602.summary: Researchers study LLM agents with emotional reasoning in an agent-based social simulation, testing whether they reproduce empirically observed emotional response patterns to events.
s87097a0602.why: Points to validated emotion-aware agent modeling for applications like emergency response and public health simulation.

sf1055fbcd0.title: Explainable Deep Learning for Malaria Parasite Detection and Species Differentiation in Thick Blood Smear Images: A Pilot Feasibility Study
sf1055fbcd0.description: arXiv:2611.31855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Species-level differentiation of Plasmodium falciparum (PF) and P. vivax (PV) determines treatment, yet deep learning detectors rarely test whether their explanations are reliable. In this pilot feasibility study of TRACE-Mal, a research prototype combining YOLOv8n-seg detection and a six-model soft-voting ensemble, we examined whether agreement among three post-hoc explanation methods (Grad-CAM, LIME and SHAP) is associated with the correctness of species calls. the study analysed 2,847 parasite crops from 250 thick smears within publicly available Lacuna Malaria Datasets. The model achieved an mAP50 score of 0.79 and the ensemble had a macro F1 of 0.84 (PF recall 0.86; PV recall 0.74). Unadjusted analyses of crops revealed that predictions
sf1055fbcd0.summary: A pilot study of TRACE-Mal examines whether agreement among Grad-CAM, LIME and SHAP explanations predicts correctness of malaria parasite species calls from blood smear images.
sf1055fbcd0.why: Shows explanation agreement may serve as a reliability signal for medical imaging classifiers, though it is a pilot feasibility study.

s31b484ba3b.title: No Fixed Configuration Is Best: Context- and Cost-Aware Tuning of LLM Pipelines, with an Application to Schema Matching and Mapping
s31b484ba3b.description: arXiv:2611.31864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The numeric settings of a multi-stage LLM pipeline (a compound AI system) are the usual target of tuning. We tuned all of them for an LLM pipeline for schema matching and mapping, with accuracy and cost as joint objectives, and we show what this buys, what it cannot buy, and where the remaining accuracy is. First, tuning buys cost and a little accuracy. On 35 tasks, with whole groups of tasks held out from tuning, one tuned configuration gains 2.9 points of top-1 accuracy (HR@1) over the default at 18% more cost, and another keeps the accuracy of the default at 32% lower cost. Second, the accuracy depends on a choice that numeric tuning cannot reach. Restricting the search for each source column to one assigned target table changes HR@1 by +3
s31b484ba3b.summary: A paper shows that tuning all settings of a multi-stage LLM schema matching pipeline for accuracy and cost yields modest accuracy gains and cost trade-offs, with no single best configuration.
s31b484ba3b.why: Indicates tuning compound LLM pipelines per context and cost budget may matter more than one fixed default configuration.

s1d74e541b4.title: RepoEviAgent: Scalable Synthesis of Evidence-Grounded Repository-Level Question Answering Tasks
s1d74e541b4.description: arXiv:2611.31873v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Real-world software engineering (SWE) tasks require agents to understand repository structures, cross-module dependencies, and runtime behaviors, posing significant challenges for constructing high-quality training and evaluation data. To address this, we propose RepoEviAgent, a scalable SWE data construction framework that integrates quality-aware data curation and role-specialized multi-agent task synthesis. Starting from 8,477 open-source repositories and approximately 2.48 million pull request records, we employ semantic alignment, complexity constraints, and multidimensional quality assessment to identify valuable SWE data. We further develop a sandbox-based multi-agent framework that integrates automated environment construction, execut
s1d74e541b4.summary: RepoEviAgent is a multi-agent framework that synthesizes evidence-grounded repository-level question-answering tasks from thousands of open-source repositories and pull requests.
s1d74e541b4.why: Offers a scalable way to build training and evaluation data for software engineering agents working across real codebases.

s70f945614d.title: HEAR, SEE, SPIKE ONCE: Highly Efficient NeuroAI Temporal Neural Networks for Low-Precision Multimodal Audio-Visual Classification and Online Learning
s70f945614d.description: arXiv:2611.31884v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spiking neural networks for multimodal audio-visual classification reach high accuracy by adopting deep-learning machinery: multi-stage convolutional or transformer encoders trained end-to-end with surrogate-gradient backpropagation through time. These prior works typically rely on full-precision (32-bit) parameters and do not treat hardware efficiency as a primary design objective. In this paper, we propose NeuTNN-AV, a much simpler hardware-amenable multimodal substrate built on the recently proposed NeuroAI Temporal Neural Network (NeuTNN) and demonstrate that it can match or outperform state-of-the-art SNN baselines with a fraction of their synapse counts. NeuTNN neurons carry multiple active dendritic segments. Each input line spikes at
s70f945614d.summary: NeuTNN-AV is a simpler, hardware-amenable spiking neural network for multimodal audio-visual classification and online learning, aiming for low-precision efficiency.
s70f945614d.why: Targets hardware efficiency as a primary design goal for multimodal neuromorphic classifiers, relevant to edge deployment.

see3246c16d.title: Cheap Memory Costs Future Compute: Co-Designing Persistent KV and GPU Execution for Efficient Streaming Video Diffusion
see3246c16d.description: arXiv:2611.31892v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Block-causal video diffusion generates long videos block by block, conditioned on a persistent key-value (KV) cache. After each block is denoised, an extra noise-free ($t=0$) forward pass writes its clean KV into the cache; once distillation and speculative early exit make denoising cheap, this clean KV update dominates the runtime. Reusing stale KV shortens the update, but stale memory corrupts the conditioning of later blocks and inflates their denoising steps, so the saved compute reappears downstream. We present SAMR (Step-Aware Memory Reconstruction), a training-free method for frozen causal video DiTs that refreshes only part of the cache and reconstructs the rest without DiT forwards. Our key observation is that, once rotary position p
see3246c16d.summary: SAMR is a method for streaming block-causal video diffusion that reconstructs stale persistent KV cache to reduce costly clean-KV update passes while preserving conditioning quality.
see3246c16d.why: Addresses a runtime bottleneck in long video generation, where cache updates dominate cost once denoising is accelerated.

s49727fe8f2.title: Contrastive On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM Unlearning
s49727fe8f2.description: arXiv:2611.31932v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model unlearning aims to remove the influence of designated training data while preserving unrelated model capabilities. Existing likelihood-based methods commonly optimize against fixed forget sequences, providing only negative supervision on what the model should not generate and overlooking the states visited by the evolving unlearned policy. We introduce Contrastive On-Policy Self-Distillation (CPSD), a new unlearning framework that constructs an explicit knowledge-reduced target distribution and distills it along the model's own trajectories. Given a student rollout, a frozen reference model evaluates each token under a plain context and a privileged context containing the forget information. CPSD treats the resulting dist
s49727fe8f2.summary: Researchers introduce Contrastive On-Policy Self-Distillation (CPSD), an LLM unlearning method that distills a knowledge-reduced target along the unlearned model's own rollouts.
s49727fe8f2.why: Offers an alternative to fixed-forget-set unlearning that may better remove training data influence while preserving other capabilities.

s950384a079.title: CAPE: Coordinating Calibration and Search for Tool-Use Policies
s950384a079.description: arXiv:2611.31938v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A tool call can fail even when the operation behind it is correct, because the receiving tool parses delimiters, dates or record layouts under a configuration the agent cannot inspect. Compiling a tool-use policy for such a tool requires both calibration, which evaluates candidate calls on candidate configurations, and search over the evaluated calls. The two share one compilation budget: calibrating everything first postpones any improved policy until the end, while re-solving every partially known model delays the next useful query. A call becomes usable as soon as its effects are known on the configurations that reach it. We present CAPE, a training-free compiler built on this observation. It maintains an executable policy at all times, di
s950384a079.summary: CAPE is a method that coordinates calibration of tool-call configurations with search over tool-use policies under a shared compilation budget.
s950384a079.why: Addresses why agent tool calls fail due to unseen tool configurations, a practical reliability issue for agent builders.

s08809b3dfa.title: Perception Is Enough, at the Right Scale: Scale-Adaptive Token Pruning for Vision-Language-Action Models
s08809b3dfa.description: arXiv:2611.31954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models must process continuous streams of visual observations, and the resulting computational cost limits real-time robotic control. Token pruning reduces this cost, but a fixed semantic scale of perceptual representation can overlook information needed at different stages of manipulation. We show that perceptual semantics can guide effective token selection without relying on internal attention when the selection scale adapts to the scene's evolving semantic structure. Based on this observation, we introduce TauPrune-VLA, a training-free method that controls the scale of the retained perceptual representation through a single perception temperature $\tau$. To adapt this scale as manipulation proceeds, TauPrune-V
s08809b3dfa.summary: TauPrune is a scale-adaptive token pruning method for vision-language-action models that selects tokens based on perceptual semantics, reducing compute for robotic control.
s08809b3dfa.why: Could lower inference cost for real-time robot control models without relying on internal attention maps.

s259f8681bd.title: DexOPD: Dual-Extrapolation On-Policy Distillation for Diffusion Models
s259f8681bd.description: arXiv:2611.31969v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Flow-based diffusion models have become a mainstream paradigm for text-to-image generation, where task-specific post-training produces specialist models with complementary strengths. Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (OPD) offers an efficient way to consolidate these specialists into a single unified student. Recent methods strengthen supervision through teacher extrapolation, constructing stronger proxy teachers that allow distilled students to surpass the original specialists. However, their extrapolation directions remain defined solely by frozen teacher and reference models, leaving the student's own training progress unexploited. To address this limitation, we introduce DexOPD, a dual-extrapolation on-policy distillation method for di
s259f8681bd.summary: DexOPD proposes dual-extrapolation on-policy distillation to consolidate multiple specialist flow-based text-to-image diffusion models into a single student model.
s259f8681bd.why: Offers a route to merge several specialist image models into one unified model that can surpass its teachers.

s5ef0c0aa6f.title: Coding4Games: Can Modern Coding Agents Play Modern Video Games?
s5ef0c0aa6f.description: arXiv:2611.31974v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Games, especially modern AAA games, challenge language models to perceive complex scenes, control actions, and make decisions over long horizons. Existing game benchmarks primarily test language models as computer-use agents that query a language model throughout play, incurring repeated inference cost and, in real-time games, acting while the environment continues to evolve. We ask whether coding agents can learn from game interaction to develop standalone game-playing programs that run without language model inference. We thus introduce Coding4Games, a benchmark for evaluating whether coding agents can develop standalone programs that play modern games through visual observations and standard game inputs. Coding4Games has three defining fea
s5ef0c0aa6f.summary: Coding4Games introduces a benchmark testing whether coding agents can learn from game interaction to build standalone programs that play modern video games without LLM inference.
s5ef0c0aa6f.why: It offers a path to game-playing programs that avoid repeated model inference costs and latency issues in real-time environments.

s0499cded43.title: Discovering Bandwidth-Efficient Prefetchers to Shrink the Cache Hierarchy
s0499cded43.description: arXiv:2611.31983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Shared last-level caches (LLCs) increasingly dominate server processor die area, forcing architects to trade core counts for cache capacity. While intelligent data prefetching offers a pathway to reclaim this silicon, designing coordinated, multi-level prefetching policies for multi-core systems is bottlenecked by day-long, cycle-level simulations. This simulation wall limits even LLM-based microarchitecture discovery; the state-of-the-art ArchAgent system evolves one cache level at a time on single-core benchmarks, adds multi-core configurations only at the end, and trails the human champion under multi-core shared cache contention. We introduce DuoArchitect, an autonomous agentic framework for multi-fidelity, multi-core co-discovery of pref
s0499cded43.summary: Researchers use LLM-based discovery to design bandwidth-efficient multi-level prefetchers that could let server processors shrink cache hierarchies.
s0499cded43.why: Shows LLM-driven microarchitecture search could help reclaim cache die area, though the excerpt gives limited detail on results.

sa70b833b71.title: How Much Dependency Can a Marginal Rule See? Total Correlation in Diffusion LM Parallel Decoding
sa70b833b71.description: arXiv:2611.31990v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A masked diffusion language model is fast because it commits several tokens per step. Each token is sampled from its own marginal, so the dependency between the tokens is lost, and the size of that loss is the conditional total correlation C of the committed set. Most decoders choose the set from per-position marginals, which can bound C but cannot determine it. We ask how well they predict it. We estimate C for fixed candidate sets on four masked diffusion LMs from two families. On three of the four, the best marginal-only predictor is off by about one bit (0.74 to 1.17), 1.8 to 3.7 times less than a baseline that knows only the bound, and most of this accuracy comes from the bound itself. On a subset, our estimate ranks sets like the exact
sa70b833b71.summary: A study measures how well marginal-only decoding rules predict the total correlation lost when masked diffusion language models commit multiple tokens per step.
sa70b833b71.why: Clarifies when parallel decoding in diffusion LMs loses accuracy, relevant to choosing decoding strategies for speed-quality tradeoffs.

s520cd7260b.title: TableRouter: Query-Aware Evidence Construction for Long-Table Question Answering
s520cd7260b.description: arXiv:2611.32006v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLMs can reason over tables, but when tables outgrow the context budget, retrieving relevant rows is only part of the solution. A retrieved subset may omit information required for an exact aggregate; even complete evidence may remain difficult for an LLM to use. We introduce TableRouter, a training-free framework that analyzes each query, then chooses between two routes: a computation route, which derives question-conditioned statistics from the full table, and a coverage route, which retrieves relevant rows and column summaries. The chosen context is passed to a frozen LLM in one call. Across three LLMs and three large-table benchmarks, TableRouter outperforms the strongest of six single-call baselines in all nine settings by 1.2-18.3 accur
s520cd7260b.summary: TableRouter is a training-free framework that routes each long-table question to either a computation route or a coverage route to build evidence for LLMs.
s520cd7260b.why: Offers a practical method to improve LLM answers over tables too large for the context window without additional training.

sce006e48c5.title: Marketing-Bench: Evaluating Frontier Models and Agents on Real-World Marketing Capabilities
sce006e48c5.description: arXiv:2611.32012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As frontier AI models and agents are deployed more broadly in the real world, marketing is emerging as one of their largest applications. Marketing teams use AI models to produce brand assets like website copy and social media posts, while consumers' agents autonomously discover products, research purchases, and navigate websites. However, evaluating marketing capability is difficult because unlike areas like software development, customer support, or legal review where ground truth is more objectively defined, marketing is subjective, and output quality is judged based on taste and brand. We introduce Marketing-Bench, the first open-source marketing benchmark, which pairs discriminative tasks (detecting brand anomalies) with generative tasks
sce006e48c5.summary: Marketing-Bench is a new benchmark for evaluating frontier models and agents on real-world marketing tasks, where ground truth is subjective.
sce006e48c5.why: Gives teams a way to assess model suitability for marketing workloads, an area where objective evaluation is hard.

sf88b32686a.title: From Rule-based to Agentic: LLM Agent based Real-time Control of Urban Drainage Systems for Flooding and Sewer Overflow Mitigation
sf88b32686a.description: arXiv:2611.32046v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Real-time control (RTC) for urban drainage systems (UDS) remains hampered by sparse in-network sensing. While heterogeneous multi-modal meteorological early warnings often contain decision-critical information for UDS RTC, none of the existing approaches can exploit such externally-sourced information within the control workflow. Here we introduce AgenticAI-Control, an agentic artificial intelligence framework able to assimilate multi-source meteorological early warnings in RTC. Two coupled large language model agents are integrated to generate control strategies by retrieving meteorological early-warnings and fusing them with domain engineering expertise. Validated via simulation studies of a combined sewer catchment in eastern China across
sf88b32686a.summary: AgenticAI-Control uses two coupled LLM agents to incorporate multi-source meteorological warnings into real-time control of urban drainage systems.
sf88b32686a.why: Demonstrates applying LLM agents to critical infrastructure control, though the excerpt provides few performance details.

s329aefbfd3.title: EffectWAM: Learning Action-Grounded Effects for Robot Manipulation
s329aefbfd3.description: arXiv:2611.32053v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: World-action models connect visual prediction with executable robot control. We present EffectWAM, which develops this connection through three complementary components: Effect, camera positional encoding (CaPE), and Action Grounding. Effect represents visual change as the difference between independently encoded future observations and a shared current-observation anchor. CaPE conditions endpoint pooling on relative camera pose when reliable extrinsics are available, while sharing the same learned parameters with pose-free pooling for uncalibrated trajectories. Action Grounding trains the visual representation to retain measured changes in end-effector pose and gripper state. An exponential moving average of the observation encoder supplies
s329aefbfd3.summary: EffectWAM is a world-action model for robot manipulation that represents visual change as effects and grounds them in executable actions using camera pose encoding.
s329aefbfd3.why: Provides a method linking visual prediction to robot control, relevant to teams building manipulation systems.

s2deefcdb3e.title: More Powerful, Less Verifiable? Mitigating Hard-to-Verify Hallucinations in MLLM's Reinforcement Learning
s2deefcdb3e.description: arXiv:2611.32055v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) strengthens model capabilities through feedback from humans and environments. However, emerging evidence suggests that reward optimization can produce outputs whose errors are harder for humans to detect. To address this issue, we construct ITHV (the Image-Text Hallucination Verifiability Dataset), comprising 2,728 visually grounded instances that distinguish between obvious hallucinations, which humans readily detect, and elusive hallucinations, which humans struggle to identify. We then propose DAPO-V, an extension of DAPO that maximizes correctness subject to a budget on verifiability-aware risk. Specifically, DAPO-V combines a verifiability-aware reward with adaptive dual control, where larger penalties are ass
s2deefcdb3e.summary: The authors build ITHV, a dataset distinguishing easy and hard-to-verify image-text hallucinations, and propose DAPO-V, an RL extension aimed at reducing the latter.
s2deefcdb3e.why: Highlights that reward optimization can yield errors humans struggle to detect, a verification risk for RL-tuned multimodal models.

s51fefaea28.title: ExpGuard: Guarding Long-Horizon LLM Agents against Corrupted Experience
s51fefaea28.description: arXiv:2611.32085v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-horizon large language model (LLM) agents distill past trajectories into reusable experiences. Misleading or adversarial guidance in source trajectories can corrupt these experiences, allowing harmful instructions to persist across tasks and influence future agent actions. Assessing the risks of potentially corrupted experiences poses three challenges: (1) modeling provenance and execution dependencies before experience reuse, (2) learning task-conditioned risk from trajectory outcomes, and (3) repairing risky experiences at online inference. To address these challenges, we present ExpGuard, a framework for retrieval-triggered experience risk assessment and online repair. Specifically, to tackle challenge (1), ExpGuard integrates experie
s51fefaea28.summary: ExpGuard is a framework that assesses and repairs corrupted experiences in long-horizon LLM agents so harmful instructions do not persist across tasks.
s51fefaea28.why: Addresses a real risk for agents that reuse past trajectories, where adversarial guidance can propagate into future actions.

s00fc3ee55d.title: From Memory Access to Evidence Sufficiency: Diagnosing and Addressing Demand--Evidence Misalignment
s00fc3ee55d.description: arXiv:2611.32088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-term memory retrieval often returns query-relevant records, but relevance does not guarantee sufficient evidence: answering requires a set of records that jointly satisfies a question's factual, relational, temporal, and state constraints. We study this demand--evidence misalignment through MemPath, an interventional framework that diagnoses failures in memory access, demand coverage, and evidence utilization. Guided by this diagnosis, we propose BiDE-Mem, which represents questions as typed demands and uses them to guide retrieval and evidence organization. We formalize demand--evidence support; in the evaluated compact path, it is conveyed through provenance-aware evidence organization and Reader guidance rather than a separate generat
s00fc3ee55d.summary: MemPath diagnoses memory retrieval failures, and BiDE-Mem uses typed demands to retrieve sets of records that jointly provide sufficient evidence for questions.
s00fc3ee55d.why: Shows relevance-based retrieval can miss needed evidence, a design concern for agent memory systems.

sa1535ee016.title: CoverMem: Coverage-Constrained Visual Memory for Budgeted Embodied Question Answering
sa1535ee016.description: arXiv:2611.32119v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Episodic-memory embodied question answering enables agents to answer questions based on previously recorded visual observations of the surrounding scenes. However, growing observation histories, varying observation quality across viewpoints, and limited computational resources make it challenging to construct and maintain compact visual memories while retrieving sufficient evidence for question answering. To address these challenges, we introduce CoverMem, which incorporates three key components: (1) a coverage-constrained memory construction method that selects a compact set of informative full frames satisfying object-quality and representative-scene coverage requirements; (2) a coverage-preserving incremental maintenance strategy that loca
sa1535ee016.summary: CoverMem is a coverage-constrained visual memory method for embodied question answering under limited computational budgets.
sa1535ee016.why: Offers ideas for keeping compact visual memories for embodied agents when observation histories grow large.

s3951081dad.title: Breaking the Binary-Lifting Barrier for DNA Minimizer Density: Exact Optimization of a Native 4-ary Order at (w, k) = (12, 5)
s3951081dad.description: arXiv:2611.32159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Minimizer schemes sample at least one $k$-mer from every window of $w$ consecutive $k$-mers via a total order $\pi$ on $\Sigma^k$. For DNA ($\sigma = 4$), state-of-the-art lookup schemes such as GreedyMini and OptMini optimize a binary order ($2^k$ ranks) and lift it to $\Sigma^k$ by ranking one bit-plane primarily and breaking $2^k$-way ties lexicographically on the other bit-plane. At $(w, k) = (12, 5)$, this projection locks sets of $32$ DNA $5$-mers into contiguous blocks and restricts the active universal hitting set (UHS) prefix to $448$ of $1024$ $5$-mers, giving exact expected DNA density $2246214544 / 2^{34} \approx 0.1307468945$ for OptMini (k5-w12-13.txt) and $2248978620 / 2^{34} \approx 0.1309077849$ for GreedyMini (w12_k5.gm). We
s3951081dad.summary: Researchers present an exact optimization of a native 4-ary order for DNA minimizer density at (w, k) = (12, 5), avoiding binary-lifting projection.
s3951081dad.why: Relevant mainly to bioinformatics sequencing tools; the excerpt offers little for general engineering teams.

sb4d1668269.title: XMind: Thinking Twice via Cross-Memory Reasoning for LLM-Based Autonomous Driving
sb4d1668269.description: arXiv:2611.32209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Memory-augmented large language model (LLM) driving agents can reuse past experience, yet previously learned corrections often fail to transfer when traffic conditions change. A key limitation is that existing memories mainly record observed outcomes, providing little evidence about alternative actions. We introduce XMind, a training-free framework that enables LLM-based driving to "Think Twice" through cross-memory reasoning. XMind integrates working memory of recent traffic states with episodic memory of critical risk events. The agent first makes an initial decision from the current context and then cross-checks it against retrieved historical experience. If a conflict arises, it makes a second decision guided by the retrieved evidence. To
sb4d1668269.summary: XMind is a training-free framework that lets LLM driving agents reason across working and episodic memories to consider alternative actions.
sb4d1668269.why: Suggests memory designs that store alternative actions could help LLM agents transfer learned corrections as traffic changes.

s1d7b2e592a.title: PoseVLN: Learning Geometric State Evolution for Vision-Language Navigation
s1d7b2e592a.description: arXiv:2611.32218v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) requires an embodied agent to relate past experience, current spatial state, and future motion while following natural-language instructions. Recent approaches improve these capabilities through long-horizon memory, state-aware reasoning, and future prediction, yet these components are often modeled separately, leaving navigation state evolution insufficiently connected across time. We argue that camera pose provides a natural geometric representation for bridging past, present, and future states. Based on this insight, we propose PoseVLN, a pose-aware VLN framework that jointly learns navigation decisions and geometric state evolution. PoseVLN organizes visual memory and the current observation in an episode-
s1d7b2e592a.summary: PoseVLN uses camera pose as a geometric representation to link past, present, and future navigation states for vision-language navigation agents.
s1d7b2e592a.why: Proposes connecting memory, state reasoning, and prediction through pose, which may inform embodied navigation system design.

s192199e400.title: Refining and Aligning Clinical Reasoning with Health Guidelines via Formal Constraints
s192199e400.description: arXiv:2611.32247v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Clinical reasoning from incomplete or conflicting patient evidence must account for low-probability but high-risk concerns while remaining grounded in health guidelines. We introduce VerClin, an explainable framework that extracts guideline conditions, exclusions, recommendations, and priorities into executable knowledge and represents patient conversations as scoped cases. A deterministic four-valued reasoner produces traceable guideline matches while preserving uncertainty and enforcing exclusions. Multiple specialty agents then screen matched guidelines for case applicability, and a consultation model synthesizes accepted guidance through specialty recommendations and a sentence-preserving formal-constraint channel. We present accepted gui
s192199e400.summary: VerClin converts health guidelines into executable knowledge and uses a four-valued deterministic reasoner with specialty agents to screen clinical cases.
s192199e400.why: Shows how formal constraints can make LLM clinical reasoning traceable, though the excerpt gives no validation results.

s83ea2a4b47.title: VC-OPD: Learning to See What Matters via Visual Cue On-Policy Self-Distillation
s83ea2a4b47.description: arXiv:2611.32292v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Visual On-Policy Distillation (OPD) commonly uses cropped or zoomed-in image regions as teacher-side privileged information to improve fine-grained perception in small Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). However, local pixel-level cues are insufficient for complex visual reasoning that requires global structure, spatial relationships, and high-level semantics. We propose Visual Cue On-Policy Self-Distillation (VC-OPD), which extends teacher-side privileged information beyond local image regions to question-conditioned visual cues. Advanced MLLMs generate cues capturing key visual details, structural relationships, and semantic evidence needed to answer each question. A multi-stage quality filtering process selects reliable cues, which a
s83ea2a4b47.summary: Researchers propose VC-OPD, an on-policy self-distillation method that uses question-conditioned visual cues beyond local crops to improve small multimodal models' visual reasoning.
s83ea2a4b47.why: Offers a training technique for small vision-language models that goes beyond zoomed-in crops, relevant to teams deploying compact multimodal models.

sa612d2ebe4.title: Sparse Poison, Strong Hijack: Efficient Trajectory-Level Backdoors in Vision-Language-Action Models with Only 1\% Poisoning
sa612d2ebe4.description: arXiv:2611.32304v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models advance robotic manipulation, but their reliance on demonstrations exposes them to backdoor threats. Among these threats, trajectory-level targeted backdoors are particularly challenging and may pose greater safety risks than behavior-disrupting attacks: rather than merely causing task failures or local action deviations, they must sustain closed-loop redirection to complete an attacker-specified multi-step task. To reliably induce such behaviors, existing methods typically rely on high poisoning rates to obtain sufficient target-trajectory supervision. However, high poisoning rates may compromise clean-task performance, whereas low rates leave target-trajectory supervision scarce and backdoor learning vuln
sa612d2ebe4.summary: A paper shows trajectory-level backdoors in vision-language-action robot models can be induced with only about 1% poisoned demonstrations, redirecting multi-step tasks.
sa612d2ebe4.why: Highlights a practical data-poisoning risk for robotic VLA models trained on demonstrations, so teams should audit training data.

sc1bfc65fe5.title: Alpha-Beta Pruning via Monadic Continuations
sc1bfc65fe5.description: arXiv:2611.32320v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Alpha-beta pruning is a fundamental technique in game-playing AI, enabling efficient minimax search by avoiding the exploration of branches that cannot affect the optimal decision. We present a monadic formulation of alpha-beta pruning based on the combination of the continuation monad and the reader monad. Unlike previous approaches that encode alpha-beta bounds into the types of available moves, our construction records these bounds within monadic outcomes, leaving the move types unchanged. We further show that the ordinary continuation monad suffices to compute not only optimal outcomes but also optimal plays, by extending the outcome type to include the corresponding sequences of moves. This provides an alternative to generalisations of t
sc1bfc65fe5.summary: A paper presents a monadic formulation of alpha-beta pruning combining the continuation and reader monads, keeping bounds in monadic outcomes rather than move types.

sbce2bb47d8.title: FigmaEval: A Benchmark for Evaluating AI Agents in Professional UI Design
sbce2bb47d8.description: arXiv:2611.32321v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in AI agents have enabled autonomous UI design using professional tools such as Figma, yet evaluating their design capabilities remains challenging due to the open-ended nature of design tasks and the absence of unique ground truths. We introduce FigmaEval, a benchmark for evaluating AI agents on professional UI design tasks, comprising 84 tasks and 783 screens derived from real-world Figma design files. FigmaEval adopts a constrained-specification, open-solution paradigm, standardizing task requirements and design resources while allowing agents to independently determine layouts, visual hierarchies, component composition, and visual presentation. To assess design quality beyond reference similarity, we develop 22 expert-grou
sbce2bb47d8.summary: FigmaEval introduces a benchmark of 84 tasks and 783 screens from real Figma files for evaluating AI agents on professional UI design work.
sbce2bb47d8.why: Gives teams a standardized way to assess whether design agents built on tools like Figma are actually useful.

s782fb494a2.title: The Control-Flow Tax: Specialized Decision Routing for LLM Agent Workflows
s782fb494a2.description: arXiv:2611.32365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An agent can spend almost as much deciding what to do as doing it. In our documentation workflow, control-flow routing accounts for 42.5% of baseline reference cost on the initial task. Lower token prices alone do not solve this control-flow tax: inexpensive general-purpose routers can trigger additional calls to the expensive generator. We evaluate a heterogeneous architecture in which Jev, a specialized System 1 decision model, controls finite actions while Sol generates documents. Across four software tasks, 480 valid runs comprise 470 completions and ten request-limit endpoints. Jev full routing achieves the lowest mean cost and elapsed time on every task, completing all 40 specialist-controlled runs along the shortest trajectory. On the
s782fb494a2.summary: A paper reports that control-flow routing consumed 42.5% of baseline reference cost in a documentation agent workflow, and proposes a specialized routing model separate from the generator.
s782fb494a2.why: Shows agent orchestration overhead can rival task cost, suggesting specialized routers as a way to cut LLM agent spend.

s45d69c097a.title: Can AI Design a Better nnU-Net? A Hypothesis-Driven Architecture Discovery Loop from Failures to Design Rules
s45d69c097a.description: arXiv:2611.32384v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural architecture search and LLM-driven evolution often reduce evaluation to a scalar fitness score, discarding failures that could explain why designs succeed or fail. We present a hypothesis-driven architecture discovery loop in which LLM agents diagnose structured error patterns, formulate falsifiable hypotheses, test counterfactual controls under a frozen nnU-Net pipeline, and distill validated mechanisms into executable trigger-to-action rules. Across eight search waves, the loop identifies two principles for 3D medical image segmentation. First, reallocating computation from high-resolution decoders to the mid-encoder preserves thin-anatomy boundaries while reducing cost. Second, support-confined region contrast addresses errors betwe
s45d69c097a.summary: Researchers describe an LLM-agent loop that diagnoses failures, tests hypotheses, and distills rules to improve nnU-Net architectures for 3D medical image segmentation.
s45d69c097a.why: Demonstrates using structured failure analysis rather than scalar fitness scores to guide automated architecture search.

se3d8157833.title: VISE: Verifier-Independent Skill Self-Evolution with Feedback from Tool Implementations
se3d8157833.description: arXiv:2611.32480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent skills provide reusable workflows that guide LLM agents in using tools. Refining these workflows requires feedback on missing or incorrect instructions, but task-specific verifiers are not always available. We propose VISE (Verifier-Independent Skill Evolution), a scripts-first approach that uses tool implementations to guide skill revision. It extracts tool capabilities, input requirements, usage conditions, and output formats from source code. Using the task request and execution trace, it compares this information with current workflow instructions to identify missing or conflicting steps. It then recommends specific edits to SKILL.md, linking each change to the relevant implementation and usage conditions. We evaluate VISE as an add
se3d8157833.summary: VISE proposes revising agent skills using tool implementation source code as feedback, without requiring task-specific verifiers.
se3d8157833.why: Offers a way to improve agent workflow instructions when no task verifier exists, reducing evaluation setup effort.

s16b10ad502.title: RecurSciBench: Benchmarking Recursive Self-Improvement in Data-Driven Scientific Research
s16b10ad502.description: arXiv:2611.32508v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents are advancing the automation of data-driven scientific research. Recent advances in recursive self-improvement (RSI) offer the potential for these agents to continuously improve through experience, but evaluating transfer across scientific tasks requires executable, scientifically verifiable tasks and independent assessment of self-improvement gains. We introduce RecurSciBench, a scalable benchmark for evaluating RSI in data-driven scientific research. Its RecurSciPipe framework automatically constructs scientific modeling and data analysis tasks from raw datasets, with execution-based verification and scientific validity checks. RecurSciBench spans four scientific domains, multiple data modalities, and
s16b10ad502.summary: RecurSciBench is a benchmark for evaluating recursive self-improvement of LLM agents on data-driven scientific research tasks.
s16b10ad502.why: Provides a framework to measure whether research agents actually improve across tasks over time.

s0765651ff1.title: A Text-to-SQL Benchmark for Official Statistics
s0765651ff1.description: arXiv:2611.32646v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Official statistics are critical datasets for a wide variety of actors, including policymakers and businesses. For providers of official statistics, improving accessibility, governance, and disclosure of their data is of key importance. This can be improved by providing question-answering systems based on text-to-SQL approaches. However, existing text-to-SQL benchmarks do not resemble this setting. Official statistics are published as open-domain catalogs of thousands of wide tables whose columns and values are codes, and whose meaning is recorded in separate metadata rather than in a relational schema. To address this gap, we introduce LOCuST, a text-to-SQL benchmark that pairs over two thousand English and Dutch tables from Statistics Nethe
s0765651ff1.summary: A new text-to-SQL benchmark targets official statistics, where data is published as thousands of wide tables with coded columns and values.
s0765651ff1.why: Reveals that standard text-to-SQL benchmarks miss the coded-schema realities of government data, a gap for enterprise data QA.

s1f25f7f2d1.title: GeoSurge: Geometry-Grounded Multimodal Reasoning for Auditable Liver Resection Planning
s1f25f7f2d1.description: arXiv:2611.32657v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Surgical resection planning centers on generating executable resection surfaces from anatomical evidence and operative constraints. Medical multimodal foundation models enable anatomical understanding, and segmentation models predict resection regions, but neither translates these capabilities into explicitly constrained, executable resection surfaces. We present GeoSurge, an anatomy-grounded framework that combines mask-derived metrics with structure-aware point-cloud tokens to generate executable, editable resection surfaces. To make resection geometry learnable and editable, GeoSurge maps actions to parametric geometry through a surface-action grammar. Using this grammar, anatomy-oriented and tumor-centered templates generate candidates, w
s1f25f7f2d1.summary: GeoSurge is a framework combining mask-derived metrics and point-cloud tokens to generate executable, editable liver resection surfaces for surgical planning.

sbcbc6e9ed7.title: Economic World Model
sbcbc6e9ed7.description: arXiv:2611.32663v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can artificial intelligence reproduce the economic dynamics that emerge as households, firms and governments interact and adapt through markets and institutions? To answer this question, we define an economic world model (EWM) as an agent's internal representation of how an economic system works, enabling counterfactual simulation and decision-making under resource constraints. We then propose a general framework for studying EWMs that links three tasks: simulating agent behaviour, learning economic transitions and systematically evaluating the dynamics. As an initial implementation, we learn household policies from microeconomic data and calibrate a structural economic transition model using macroeconomic data, linking individual decisions t
sbcbc6e9ed7.summary: The paper defines an economic world model as an agent's internal representation of economic dynamics and proposes a framework to simulate and evaluate it.

s875a747b9f.title: CAPTA: Identifying LLMs Behind AI Agents
s875a747b9f.description: arXiv:2611.32686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents access remote services through tools to complete user tasks, often via API calls. In this setting, a remote service may want to identify the backend LLM of an agent to launch model-specific attacks, including prompt injection or selective delivery of manipulated content. However, the service cannot directly query the backend model and must instead collect observable responses through its interactions with the agent, making identification challenging. In this paper, we present Completely Automated Preference Test to tell LLMs Apart (CAPTA), a model identification approach inspired by CAPTCHA (Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart), which distinguishes humans from auto
s875a747b9f.summary: CAPTA is a method for identifying which backend LLM powers an AI agent by observing its responses through tool-mediated interactions.
s875a747b9f.why: Shows remote services can fingerprint underlying models, relevant to security threat modeling for agent APIs.

sabdc42110e.title: EviCraft: Can Minecraft Agents Find What They Cannot See?
sabdc42110e.description: arXiv:2611.32765v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In Minecraft, a common testbed for embodied agents, semantic tools such as mineBlock pick targets from the simulator's loaded world state without a visibility test, so a buried ore the agent has never seen is one call away, and scores cannot show whether the agent searched. We formalize the missing requirement as evidence closure: every decision of an agent system, including those inside its tools, may depend on the world only through facts for which the agent holds evidence. EviCraft is a runtime and benchmark that enforces closure below the agent and makes the admission rule an experimental variable: a perception-grounded regime (G) admits only what is in line of sight or returned by the agent's own actions, and a loaded-state regime (L) re
sabdc42110e.summary: EviCraft is a Minecraft runtime and benchmark that enforces evidence closure, so agents and their tools can only use world facts the agent has observed.
sabdc42110e.why: Addresses a flaw where agent tools access hidden simulator state, making evaluations misleadingly high.

s590287cd9a.title: RubikSQL-HB: Agentic Text-to-SQL with Knowledge in the Loop
s590287cd9a.description: arXiv:2611.32772v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Database agents need more than schema structure: business meanings, stored values and reference queries supply knowledge that becomes relevant at different points in reasoning. We introduce RubikSQL-HB, which exposes these materials through queryable, database-specific knowledge workspaces built on the HeavenBase platform. Its knowledge interface remains available as an agent constructs and investigates an answer. Candidate agents interleave knowledge access with SQL construction and execution; a downstream Judge can reuse the same interfaces to investigate disagreements. A two-stage example interface separates discovering a reference question from expanding its SQL. On a 500-question BIRD Mini-Dev evaluation, the full pipeline reaches 75.2%
s590287cd9a.summary: RubikSQL-HB gives text-to-SQL agents queryable, database-specific knowledge workspaces covering business meanings, stored values and reference queries throughout reasoning.
s590287cd9a.why: Shows how exposing business knowledge interactively during SQL generation may improve database agents over schema-only approaches.

sb97c8d6c37.title: Learning World Models through Contrastive Identification of Actions
sb97c8d6c37.description: arXiv:2611.32776v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Latent world models enable goal-directed planning from offline visual data, but prediction alone does not specify which action-related distinctions their representations should preserve. Inverse dynamics provides auxiliary supervision, yet squared-error action regression rewards additional information only through changes in the conditional action mean. We propose Contrastive Identification of Actions (CIA), which identifies the executed action among alternatives sampled from a history-conditioned behavior proposal. Comparing actions plausible in the same context targets information supplied by the next latent beyond history. Under exact behavior matching, we show that CIA can reward action information that leaves optimal inverse-regression e
sb97c8d6c37.summary: The paper proposes Contrastive Identification of Actions (CIA), a training objective for latent world models that identifies the executed action among alternatives.
sb97c8d6c37.why: Offers an alternative to squared-error inverse dynamics for learning action-relevant representations in offline visual planning.

s723d67b943.title: Accuracy of Noise Ceiling Estimators for Brain Scores
s723d67b943.description: arXiv:2611.32792v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The internal activations of modern machine learning models align surprisingly well with the activities recorded in real brains. In the last five years, the alignment between encoding models and brain activities, often called brain scores, has steadily increased. Because brain recordings are noisy, there exists an upper bound to the brain scores that any model can achieve. This bound, called the noise ceiling, is crucial for two reasons: it determines whether further improvements in model performance are possible, and it enables meaningful comparisons of brain scores across benchmarks. The field has developed multiple approaches to estimate noise ceilings, but the statistical properties of existing estimators remain poorly understood, leaving
s723d67b943.summary: Researchers examine how accurate noise ceiling estimators are for brain scores, which bound how well models can match neural recordings.
s723d67b943.why: Gives evaluators of brain-alignment benchmarks a clearer sense of whether reported model gains are meaningful or near the measurement limit.

s098e96e6d5.title: Interactive Neural Computers
s098e96e6d5.description: arXiv:2611.32811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computers and their interfaces are usually treated as fixed, so a person, or increasingly an AI agent, must adapt to whatever the operating system presents. This is limiting when someone needs a different workflow, or an interface suited to hands-free use or a disability. We explore an overlooked alternative. Rather than training an agent to operate an existing computer, we train a generative model to be the computer, predicting each next screen from past screens and the user's mouse and keyboard actions. Treating a desktop as an interactive world model raises problems that natural-video world models largely avoid. Without a camera pose to index memory, the model must remember content that has left the screen without any geometric cues. Arith
s098e96e6d5.summary: Researchers propose training a generative model to act as the computer itself, predicting each next screen from past screens and user inputs.
s098e96e6d5.why: Suggests an alternative to agents operating fixed interfaces, which could enable customizable or accessibility-focused computing workflows.

sf8f4002206.title: Measurement Artifacts in Trustworthiness Evaluations of Quantized Small Language Models
sf8f4002206.description: arXiv:2611.32848v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evaluations of quantized language models attribute the change in a benchmark score to quantization. We write the measured change as the true change plus a term contributed by the instrument. Instrument error that is the same at every precision can shrink a paired comparison but cannot create or reverse an effect. Error that interacts with quantization can do both, and it is reported as an effect of quantization. We estimate this interaction for four measurement choices in 8 instruction-tuned models below two billion parameters, at float16, LLM.int8() and NF4, on identical items. Measured against labels from two human annotators, the 4-bit rise in harmful compliance is about half to two-thirds of the rise in non-refusal that a corrected key wo
sf8f4002206.summary: A study finds instrument error can interact with quantization to create apparent effects on trustworthiness benchmarks of small quantized language models.
sf8f4002206.why: Teams comparing quantized models on trust or safety benchmarks may be misattributing score changes to quantization rather than to measurement artifacts.

s3d12a70e86.title: Lazy Agents Answer Against Their Own Beliefs: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Beliefs Teaches Them to Act on What They Believe
s3d12a70e86.description: arXiv:2611.32884v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents working on long tasks often commit to an answer before they have enough evidence, a behavior called laziness. In our evaluations, they frequently commit even while their stated belief still names several possible answers. An outcome reward at the end of the episode scores only the final answer, so it cannot teach the agent when to commit, because a lucky guess receives the same reward as an answer backed by evidence. During training, however, the simulator can compute the exact posterior over the answer at every step and tell whether the evidence is already enough. We propose Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Beliefs (RLVB), which rewards the agent for taking further steps while this posterior still allows several answers and f
s3d12a70e86.summary: Researchers propose reinforcement learning with verifiable beliefs to teach AI agents to commit to answers only when evidence supports them.
s3d12a70e86.why: Addresses premature answer commitment in long-horizon agents, a reliability problem for engineers building agentic systems that must decide when to act.

s31f1d742e9.title: InstructReplay: Replaying Assistant Turns to Preserve General Behavior During Factual Fine-Tuning
s31f1d742e9.description: arXiv:2611.32918v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fine-tuning an instruction-tuned language model on new facts often erodes its general abilities. We find that standard fine-tuning lowers instruction-following, reasoning and coding benchmarks by 35 points on average, and that these losses track a collapse in answer length: fine-tuned models at least halve their responses, and the further a response drifts from the initial model's length, the more often it fails. We propose InstructReplay: the initial model answers a set of general instructions once, and during fine-tuning the model is kept close to the initial model on these answers. Across three model families and two domains, InstructReplay reduces the average decline on five general benchmarks from 28.1 to 2.4 points and keeps answer leng
s31f1d742e9.summary: InstructReplay is proposed to keep instruction-tuned models' general behavior intact during factual fine-tuning by replaying assistant turns.
s31f1d742e9.why: Reports that standard fine-tuning cut instruction-following, reasoning and coding scores by about 35 points on average, a practical risk when updating models with new facts.

sbdc523c87e.title: Reading Decisions Before Spans: Efficient Generative Verification
sbdc523c87e.description: arXiv:2611.32931v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A developer checking an assistant's report may need only an alarm that a claim is unsupported. A generative verifier, however, can continue decoding to quote and classify the errors. We study how much of that output is needed to recover its decision. In a frozen 2B span verifier, the choice between an empty error list and its first object precedes all localization. Native8 stops generation at this branch. The preceding seven syntax tokens are fixed, so Prefill1 supplies them as input and generates only the unrestricted branch token, using the same native instruction. On 2,015 code-agent TEST responses, Prefill1 reduces eager resident service by 84.84% relative to full generation, with released-reference F1 of 83.43 versus 83.41. It saves 31.9
sbdc523c87e.summary: Researchers show a generative verifier's accept-or-error decision can be recovered from early output tokens, avoiding full decoding for claim checking.
sbdc523c87e.why: Could lower latency and compute for teams running generative verifiers that only need a pass or fail alarm on claims.

s63aad5f945.title: ShellBench: What Matters More for AI Agents, Models, or Harness for Everyday Tasks
s63aad5f945.description: arXiv:2611.32946v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The use of AI agents among the general public has been increasing exponentially throughout 2026, though it is often hard for users to determine which configuration is most effective for their personal use. To help provide clarity here we introduce ShellBench, 100 day-to-day tasks based on more than 10 million user requests, each set in a realistic workspace with messy files and competing data sources, and graded for both correctness and safety. We evaluate 12 models across 5 agent harnesses at 3 reasoning levels for a total of 53,100 rollouts, 20% of which are on tasks designated for public release. We find that model choice impacts performance more than harness choice, but the three leading models differ by only 1.1 percentage points. GPT-6.
s63aad5f945.summary: ShellBench introduces 100 everyday tasks to compare how models and agent harnesses affect correctness and safety, evaluating 12 models across 5 harnesses.
s63aad5f945.why: Offers evidence on whether model choice or agent harness matters more for everyday agent tasks, informing configuration decisions.

s1cba622c8f.title: Beyond Expected Value: PPO with Distributional Critics for Systematic Conservation Planning
s1cba622c8f.description: arXiv:2611.32948v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Systematic conservation planning must allocate limited protection budgets sequentially under ecological and climatic uncertainty. Static tools cannot adapt as conditions change, and policies optimised only for expected outcomes can fail on the worst-case trajectories climate change makes increasingly likely. CAPTAIN was the first framework to cast this as sequential reinforcement learning, but its gradient-free Evolution Strategies (ES) optimiser lacks per-timestep credit assignment. We replace ES with Proximal Policy Optimisation (PPO) via a Plackett-Luce solution to CAPTAIN's non-differentiable action space, and replace its scalar critic with an Implicit Quantile Network (IQN) modelling the full return distribution. A matched-granularity co
s1cba622c8f.summary: Researchers replace evolution strategies with PPO and distributional critics in CAPTAIN, a sequential reinforcement learning framework for conservation planning.
s1cba622c8f.why: Shows how distributional critics can address worst-case outcomes in sequential planning under uncertainty, though the application is domain-specific.

s2bcf1650c0.title: LoomKV: Lossless KV Cache Compression from GPU Memory to SSD for LLM Serving
s2bcf1650c0.description: arXiv:2611.32954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) serving engines offload the key/value (KV) cache from GPU memory to host DRAM and SSD so multi-turn and agent requests can reuse prompt prefixes. Capacity then limits service at two levels: external tiers govern prefix reuse before eviction, while the GPU KV pool bounds concurrent long requests, and lossy compression alters KV values and outputs. LoomKV brings lossless KV compression to both external tiers (tier mode) and the GPU pool (pool mode) on an unmodified engine. Using a calibrated per-head two-level 3-bit code over BF16 high bytes (sign and upper seven exponent bits), LoomKV stores BF16 KV at 0.71 of its raw size across nine models and FP8 KV at 0.85-0.87. In tier mode, TileStream writes exact-length record
s2bcf1650c0.summary: LoomKV proposes lossless KV cache compression spanning GPU memory, host DRAM and SSD for LLM serving on unmodified engines.
s2bcf1650c0.why: Lossless KV offloading to SSD could raise concurrency and prefix reuse for long-context and agent serving without changing outputs.

scf518275b3.title: Can LLM Judges Catch Unsafe Clinical Actions? A Fault-Injection Study
scf518275b3.description: arXiv:2611.33012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As clinical AI agents begin to interact with electronic health records (EHRs), large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to evaluate their actions. But how reliably can these judges recognize clinically dangerous mistakes, especially when an agent appears to have completed its task successfully? We investigate this question using MedAgentBench by introducing controlled clinical errors into verified agent trajectories. The experiments include 416 faulty trajectories, eight error categories, and six open-weight LLM judges. By comparing each faulty trajectory with its correct counterpart, we measure whether judges genuinely recognize errors rather than simply flagging more actions as unsafe. The findings show that access to clinical evi
scf518275b3.summary: A fault-injection study tests whether six open-weight LLM judges can detect unsafe clinical actions in MedAgentBench agent trajectories.
scf518275b3.why: Indicates LLM judges may miss dangerous clinical errors even when agents appear to finish tasks, a caution for evaluating healthcare agents.

s4135a1dd13.title: RecordRoute: Auditing Agent Failures with Localization-Guided Diagnosis
s4135a1dd13.description: arXiv:2611.33022v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Auditing failed agent executions requires identifying the responsible actor, the earliest decisive step, and the error mode. Representative supervised methods either focus on step localization or predict multiple attribution targets from shared trajectory representations. These methods do not use the localization result to select the text for mode diagnosis. To address this limitation, we propose RecordRoute, which couples comparative localization with local diagnosis. Specifically, it represents each record with word and character features and learns to rank records through comparisons within each trajectory. The selected record supplies the actor and step, while its text and metadata drive mode prediction. On controlled-injection Who&When P
s4135a1dd13.summary: RecordRoute proposes couples localization with diagnosis to audit failed agent executions, identifying the responsible actor, decisive step and error mode.
s4135a1dd13.why: Offers a method for post-hoc debugging of failed agent runs, which matters for teams operating multi-step agents in production.

s095a984fa4.title: Hybrid AI for AI-Native RAN Control: A Functional Perspective
s095a984fa4.description: arXiv:2611.33035v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI-native radio access network (RAN) control involves interdependent decisions across network entities, protocol layers, and timescales. Understanding how AI and conventional methods can jointly support these decisions requires a common basis for comparing their functional roles. This survey introduces a technique-agnostic taxonomy of RAN decision-making organized around four complementary capabilities: Representation and Reasoning, Prediction and Simulation, Adaptive Control, and Decision Synthesis. These capabilities are defined by their roles in the control process, independently of the techniques used to implement them.
