s8e47591890.title: DELTA: Diagnosing Exploration Lineages via Twin-path Alignment - What Can Contrasting Design Paths Reveal About Microarchitectural Behavior?
s8e47591890.description: arXiv:2611.31767v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Architects have two mature instruments for performance work. Top-Down analysis tells them where a design loses its pipeline slots, and design-space exploration (DSE) tells them which configuration scores best. Neither explains why a search stops improving: why a backend-bound design rejects a prefetcher that the bottleneck label recommends, or why a capacity increase that helped in one configuration hurts in the next. This paper argues that the evidence needed to answer such questions is already produced during exploration and then discarded. Every parent-child edge in an exploration tree is a controlled intervention: one knob changes, the rest of the design is held fixed, and a cycle-level simulator measures the outcome. When the same edit
s8e47591890.summary: The DELTA paper proposes using data produced during design-space exploration to explain why microarchitecture searches stop improving.
s8e47591890.why: It suggests architects can reuse exploration traces to diagnose bottlenecks, not just pick the best configuration.

scfe6ef0847.title: SPARQL-Planned Single-Hop Traversal over a Live Knowledge Graph for Multi-Hop Question Answering
scfe6ef0847.description: arXiv:2611.31771v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Semantic retrieval struggles with multi-hop question answering on both recall and precision: gold passages are buried among distractors that degrade the reader's answer, and retrieving them requires reasoning over the query rather than matching it. GraphRAG techniques expand semantic retrieval by connecting passages to graph nodes and performing one or more hops of expansion after initial retrieval. This improves recall, but multi-hop expansion becomes expensive and brings additional noise into the retrieved set. We break this tradeoff by \emph{interleaving} dense retrieval with knowledge-graph traversal for complex multi-hop questions. Dense retrieval locates the first relevant regions of the search space at good recall, while traversal of
scfe6ef0847.summary: The paper proposes SPARQL-planned single-hop traversal over a live knowledge graph to improve multi-hop question answering retrieval.
scfe6ef0847.why: It offers a way to reduce the noise and cost of multi-hop graph expansion in retrieval-augmented systems.

s67cf98cd35.title: VISOR: A Vision-Language Selector for Multimodal Time-Series Forecasting
s67cf98cd35.description: arXiv:2611.31780v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent time-series foundation models (TSFMs) forecast a distribution over futures, and multimodal time-series (TS) forecasting further exploits other modalities to improve forecasting accuracy. However, existing works have two limitations: 1) TSFMs reduce the predictive distribution to its median or mean, flattening diverse futures into a calm line, and 2) multimodal TS forecasting models incorporate text into the forecaster through TS-language alignment, which is substantially weaker than vision-language alignment. To address these limitations, we propose the VIsion-language SelectOR (VISOR), a multimodal TS forecasting framework that selects one plausible future instead of averaging across candidates, leveraging the alignment capabilities
s67cf98cd35.summary: VISOR is a vision-language selector for multimodal time-series forecasting that aims to preserve diverse future distributions rather than collapsing to a median.
s67cf98cd35.why: It targets two named limits of current forecasters: flattened predictive distributions and weak text-to-series alignment.

sc0d9018f46.title: Three-Dimensional Wake Reconstruction and Cross-Scale Transfer for Floating Offshore Wind Turbines via Physics-Informed Fourier Neural Operators
sc0d9018f46.description: arXiv:2611.31789v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coupled surge-pitch motions drive unsteady vortex interactions and dynamic wake meandering behind floating offshore wind turbines, complicating three-dimensional wake reconstruction from limited measurements and transfer across turbine scales. Large-eddy simulations coupled with an actuator line model generate fixed and surge-pitch wakes at motion-based Strouhal numbers $St=fD/U_\infty$ of 0.2-0.6 (where $f$, $D$, and $U_\infty$ are the motion frequency, rotor diameter, and inflow velocity) for the National Renewable Energy Laboratory 5 MW ($D=126$ m) and International Energy Agency 22 MW ($D=284$ m) turbines. A physics-informed Fourier neural operator framework combines four-dimensional spectral convolutions with incompressible continuity
sc0d9018f46.summary: Researchers used physics-informed Fourier neural operators to reconstruct three-dimensional wakes behind floating offshore wind turbines and transfer them across turbine scales.

saa6875e256.title: Learning Compact State Abstractions for LLM Agents
saa6875e256.description: arXiv:2611.31800v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM agents commonly use the full interaction history as a proxy for state, retaining all past observations and actions regardless of whether they remain relevant. We instead ask what information an agent actually needs to carry forward. We define agent state as a compact abstraction of interaction history that preserves the competence of a fixed reference agent, with the minimal such abstraction as the ideal. Because matching the reference agent's behavior is unnecessarily restrictive and difficult for black-box policies, we define sufficiency through task performance rather than behavior matching. We represent state abstractions as deterministic recursive programs and search over them using an LLM-guided genetic algorithm. Across ALFWorld
saa6875e256.summary: The paper defines compact state abstractions that let LLM agents keep only the interaction history they need, instead of the full history.
saa6875e256.why: Smaller agent state could cut context costs while keeping a reference agent's competence, relevant to long-running agent design.

sec7b84fb64.title: TopoCryptoEEG: End-to-End Encrypted Framework for Brainprint Authentication
sec7b84fb64.description: arXiv:2611.31801v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Brainprint authentication enables continuous identity verification, but EEG data are privacy-sensitive. Existing feature-level encrypted authentication (FLEA) schemes protect extracted features under a trusted-client assumption. We show theoretically and empirically that a compromised client with access to plaintext query features and continuous authentication scores can exactly recover a registered template after finitely many interactions. To address this risk, we propose TopoCryptoEEG, a homomorphic-encryption-based framework that encrypts preprocessed EEG data at the client and performs feature extraction, template matching, score computation, and threshold centering on ciphertexts at the server. This extends protection from extracted f
sec7b84fb64.summary: TopoCryptoEEG proposes a homomorphic-encryption framework for brainprint authentication after showing encrypted feature schemes can leak templates.
sec7b84fb64.why: It highlights that feature-level encryption under a trusted-client assumption can be broken, a design concern for biometric systems.

s95aa62d82c.title: How Far Apart Are Two Proofs? Measuring Proof Dissimilarity in a Proof Kernel and in Lean/Mathlib
s95aa62d82c.description: arXiv:2611.31811v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We now live in the age of machine-generated mathematics: AI systems produce research-level proofs faster than the human mathematical community can read them. Verification is only part of the challenge. We also need to know whether a "new proof" is indeed new, whether a thousand generated proofs contain one idea or many, and where each sits relative to human mathematics. All of these require measuring distances between proofs. Following Hilbert's 24th problem and the identity-of-proofs problem, we ask how far apart two proofs of one theorem are, and what shape the proof space they inhabit has. We define 19 dissimilarity measures in 6 families (syntactic, structural, dependency & resource, semantic, information-theoretic, higher-categorical)
s95aa62d82c.summary: The paper introduces methods for measuring distances between mathematical proofs, in a proof kernel and in Lean/Mathlib.
s95aa62d82c.why: Proof-distance metrics could help teams judge whether AI-generated formal proofs are actually novel or redundant.

s17c863b611.title: Agentic Discovery of Soundness Bugs in Safe Rust Bindings
s17c863b611.description: arXiv:2611.31813v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rust crates confine unsafe code, such as calls into C or C++ libraries or system calls, behind safe interfaces that must uphold Rust's invariants. If an interface encodes one rule of the code beneath it too weakly, a program written in purely safe Rust can cause undefined behavior. Static analyzers and fuzzers are bound to fixed patterns or to the paths they execute. We propose LLM agents as auditors of these interfaces, and study how well they do it. We first define a taxonomy of the defects of such interfaces, including undefined behavior, divergences from the wrapped library, and incomplete unsafe contracts. We then measure, in repeated audits of a real-world crate by a closed and an open model, Claude Opus 5.5 and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, w
s17c863b611.summary: The paper proposes using LLM agents to audit safe Rust bindings for soundness bugs that allow undefined behavior from safe code.
s17c863b611.why: Agentic auditing of Rust FFI wrappers could find unsafe-boundary defects that static analyzers and fuzzers miss.

s89150f6103.title: Exploring Multi-Player Social Games as Verifiable Training Grounds for Large Language Models
s89150f6103.description: arXiv:2611.31821v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The training of socially intelligent language models often relies on large language model (LLM) judges, which are expensive, noisy, and vulnerable to reward hacking. Multi-player social games offer a natural alternative: they require open-ended communication to coordinate with teammates and infer hidden roles, while their rules provide an objective outcome which can serve as a verifiable reward for training. Using three social games, we explore how much social intelligence Qwen3 models can acquire through supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). Results show that against a much stronger Gemma-3-27B model, SFT and RLVR raise the win rate of Qwen3-4B from 33% to 81% on the three trained games, an
s89150f6103.summary: The paper explores multi-player social games as verifiable training environments for Qwen3 models using SFT and reinforcement learning.
s89150f6103.why: Rule-based game outcomes could replace expensive, noisy LLM judges as reward signals for social-skill training.

sa49022e63f.title: POISE: Curvature-Aware Critic Regularization for Smooth Actor-Critic Control
sa49022e63f.description: arXiv:2611.31835v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Actor-critic methods achieve high returns in robotic control, yet trained actors exhibit high-frequency action oscillations. Most smoothness methods constrain the actor, whereas PAVE regularizes the critic by separately penalizing action-gradient variation and encouraging negative action curvature. The same gradient change, however, moves the critic's preferred action farther where the critic is flat, and separate penalties do not measure this motion. We characterize this motion through the greedy shift, which approximates greedy-action displacement across state transitions to first order under local concavity. Since displacement alone does not reflect its critic-value consequences, the analysis further shows that the shift's curvature-weig
sa49022e63f.summary: POISE proposes curvature-aware critic regularization to reduce high-frequency action oscillations in actor-critic robotic control.
sa49022e63f.why: It targets smoothness of learned robot controllers by regularizing the critic rather than the actor.

s4bad0adb6a.title: Gaze World Model
s4bad0adb6a.description: arXiv:2611.31836v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Where a person looks indicates their focus of attention, and how their gaze shifts between targets reveals how that attention responds to a changing scene. Existing gaze target estimation methods largely operate frame by frame and do not model these shifts. Gaze shifts are often driven by dynamic changes in the scene, which is the kind of information world models are designed to encode. This relationship is subtle, however, since an event far across the frame may produce only a slight movement of the person's head or eyes. We therefore introduce the Gaze World Model (GWM), which co-trains latent scene prediction with person-conditioned gaze supervision on a frozen V-JEPA 2.1 encoder; in our ablations, the latent prediction objective improve
s4bad0adb6a.summary: The Gaze World Model paper introduces a world-model approach to estimating gaze targets and how gaze shifts respond to scene changes.

s7840c669cd.title: Spec-Test Coverage Gap: Detecting Overspecified Tests in SWE-Bench-Style Benchmarks
s7840c669cd.description: arXiv:2611.31839v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: SWE-bench-style benchmarks, such as SWE-bench Verified (Verified) and SWE-bench Pro (Pro), evaluate coding agents with tests taken from the change that originally fixed each issue. However, these tests can enforce details the task never states, causing correct alternative fixes to fail. Such overspecified tests have so far been found mainly through expensive expert review. To address this, we define the Spec-Test Coverage Gap (STCG), a 1-4 scale measuring overspecification, and score it with two LLM judges, Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol, which are given the specification and the test patch. A task is flagged as overspecified when both judges score it 3 or higher. Our study has three parts. First, we validate the judges on 206 tasks that e
s7840c669cd.summary: The paper defines a Spec-Test Coverage Gap metric and uses LLM judges to detect overspecified tests in SWE-bench-style coding benchmarks.
s7840c669cd.why: Overspecified tests can reject correct alternative fixes, so this affects how reliably coding-agent benchmarks measure performance.

sdf38b43940.title: Faithful Persona Steering under Incongruity via Dual-Stream Refinement
sdf38b43940.description: arXiv:2611.31848v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Standard LLM personalization typically frames identity as a static retrieval task, overlooking the inherent incongruity of human personas, where stable traits coexist with atypical, context-specific stances. Existing methods struggle to reconcile these dimensions: prompting succumbs to context drift over long sequences, while fine-tuning often suppresses idiosyncratic "quirks" in favor of generic distributional patterns. To bridge this gap, we present QuirkyMind, a framework that disentangles identity definition from its expression. First, Traits Anchoring constructs a dual-stream latent state, fusing a sentence-level summary for semantic stability with a token-level sequence for generative control. This state is stabilized via In-Context N
sdf38b43940.summary: QuirkyMind is a framework that separates persona identity definition from its expression to keep atypical persona traits in LLM steering.
sdf38b43940.why: It addresses context drift and loss of idiosyncratic traits in long-sequence LLM personalization.

s86a2c35c91.title: JECT: Addressing the Context Shortcut in Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning for Chest CT
s86a2c35c91.description: arXiv:2611.31849v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Joint-embedding predictive architectures learn by predicting features of masked regions from visible context. In chest computed tomography, the findings that decide a diagnosis, such as a small nodule, are often not predictable from the surrounding anatomy. A hidden finding is then best predicted toward normal anatomy, and the prediction loss stops rewarding the encoder for representing it. We call this the context shortcut. Conditioning the predictor on the radiology report repairs the prediction, but in our setup the encoder gains little over image-only pretraining: the report supplies what the encoder never had to learn. JECT therefore gives the report two roles: a condition for the predictor and, through masked section-text prediction,
s86a2c35c91.summary: JECT addresses a context shortcut in joint-embedding predictive learning for chest CT, where hidden findings are predicted as normal anatomy.

s9cfab3ad80.title: Two-Stage Post-Training for Flow-Based Embodied Foundation Models
s9cfab3ad80.description: arXiv:2611.31850v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large-scale pretraining provides embodied models with general capabilities, but reliable task execution still requires post training. In multitask settings, supervised fine-tuning (SFT) faces distribution mismatch between training and deployment, whereas reinforcement learning (RL) is limited by sparse rewards and uneven learning progress across tasks. Multi-teacher on policy distillation (MOPD) consolidates expert capabilities through dense supervision on the model's own trajectories, but achieving performance beyond the teachers remains challenging. We propose a two-stage post training framework for flow-based embodied models, constructing distillation objectives from the velocity regression formulation of conditional flow matching. Stage
s9cfab3ad80.summary: An arXiv paper proposes a two-stage post-training approach for flow-based embodied foundation models, building on multi-teacher on-policy distillation to go beyond teacher performance.
s9cfab3ad80.why: Offers a post-training recipe for robot foundation models that aims to combine supervised fine-tuning and RL while mitigating distribution mismatch and sparse rewards.

s59b7cf97be.title: CALVIN-MAX: When Does a Mid-Execution Change Hurt a Robot Policy?
s59b7cf97be.description: arXiv:2611.31868v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Robots must often keep working after the world changes, as when a block moves or the camera shifts while the robot still acts on what it saw before. Recent work showed that one change during a task lowers success for every policy tested, but did not separate the effect of its timing from the cost of the changed world, or measure what it costs afterwards. We introduce CALVIN-MAX, a benchmark of 7,828 cases on CALVIN's five-instruction chains, each with one change to the objects, the camera, the robot, or the instruction. Each case compares three runs that are identical until the affected instruction begins: one without the change, one with it in place from that moment, and one in which it arrives while the robot is moving. The second run aga
s59b7cf97be.summary: Researchers introduce CALVIN-MAX, a benchmark of 7,828 cases testing how a single mid-task change to objects, camera, robot, or instruction affects robot policy success.
s59b7cf97be.why: Gives teams a benchmark for measuring robot policy robustness to mid-execution environment changes, a common failure mode in deployment.

sdb33355120.title: EEG-Jev: A Unified Single-Pass Decision Model for EEG
sdb33355120.description: arXiv:2611.31875v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: EEG analysis spans choosing alternatives, judging statements, and rating ordered attributes, requiring calibratable probabilities with explicit meaning. We present EEG-Jev, a unified single-pass decision model for EEG. Given an EEG window, a question and an answer specification, one forward pass returns a typed readout: CHOICE gives a candidate distribution, NOUL a proposition probability, and SCORE an ordered-level distribution and expectation. One checkpoint is trained jointly and evaluated once on held-out splits of 35 public sources. Core raw outputs reach 54.08% balanced accuracy on Stieger2021 motor imagery, 70.45% on Sleep-EDF-SC sleep staging, 72.11% per window at threshold 0.5 on CHB-MIT seizure detection with 0.825 AUROC, and 1.70
sdb33355120.summary: EEG-Jev is a unified single-pass model that handles EEG choice, statement judgment, and ordered rating tasks, trained jointly on 35 public sources.

scb469b3813.title: Rethinking Video Agents: When and Why Video Harnesses Work
scb469b3813.description: arXiv:2611.31883v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Video understanding depends not only on how models reason about visual evidence, but also on which evidence they observe. Fixed observation policies determine this evidence in advance; agentic harnesses allow models to seek further observations as their understanding develops. This shift creates an opportunity to realize capabilities that fixed inputs leave untapped, yet the ability to request observations does not ensure their effective use. We investigate when and why video harnesses improve understanding, examining how task demands and models' capacity for interaction jointly shape their benefits. Using Video-Relook as an experimental framework, we let models adapt their temporal and spatial observations from a common default configurati
scb469b3813.summary: A paper examines when and why agentic video harnesses, which let models request further observations, improve video understanding compared with fixed input policies.
scb469b3813.why: Suggests that letting models request more video evidence only helps under certain task and model conditions, which affects agent design choices.

s65d3675b8d.title: Loupe: Reinforcing Knowledge-Intensive Video Generation Agents
s65d3675b8d.description: arXiv:2611.31895v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Knowledge-intensive video generation remains challenging because prompts often omit the facts, appearances, and temporal relationships required for accurate generation. While search-based workflows can retrieve missing evidence, manually designed strategies limit adaptive planning, and conventional training suffers from costly video-level feedback and coarse trajectory-level credit assignment. In this paper, we present Loupe, a video generation agent that retrieves and verifies textual and visual evidence to construct evidence-grounded temporal video prompts with reference images. We further introduce Rubric-Based Credit (RBC), which leverages prompt-specific factual, visual, and temporal requirements to evaluate intermediate search and pla
s65d3675b8d.summary: Loupe is a video generation agent that retrieves and verifies textual and visual evidence to build evidence-grounded plans for knowledge-intensive video generation, trained with reinforcement learning.
s65d3675b8d.why: Shows an agentic retrieval-and-verification loop for improving factual accuracy in generated video, relevant to teams building generative media pipelines.

s9e94bd535f.title: MIFLOW: Dynamic Recent-Behavior Priors for Reference-Calibrated Online Flow-Policy Reinforcement Learning
s9e94bd535f.description: arXiv:2611.31902v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Flow-based policies provide expressive action distributions for continuous-control reinforcement learning. In online actor-critic learning, off-policy value estimates can be unreliable in poorly covered action regions, where expressive policies may shift probability mass toward critic-favored actions. We propose MIFLOW, which calibrates online flow-policy learning with a recency-adaptive flow-matching prior fitted to recently executed actions. Inspired by canalization as a qualitative analogy for path-dependent stabilization, we use the prior as a moving density reference for value-guided policy improvement. MIFLOW uses the approximate recent-action log-density in a dimension-normalized correction to both actor updates and critic targets. T
s9e94bd535f.summary: MIFLOW proposes a recency-adaptive flow-matching prior fitted to recently executed actions to calibrate online flow-policy reinforcement learning for continuous control.

sf192459b5b.title: Your VLM Knows What to Inspect: Semantic Probe-Guided Adaptive Focusing for GUI Grounding
sf192459b5b.description: arXiv:2611.31909v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: GUI grounding requires resolving fine visual details within the context that gives them meaning. Additional views can improve localization, but their value depends on what evidence they expose and how much context they preserve. We explore a capability of vision-language models (VLMs): even when their coordinate predictions are incorrect, they can describe visual evidence worth inspecting. We introduce \textbf{SPARK}, \textit{\textbf{S}emantic \textbf{P}robe-guided \textbf{A}daptive \textbf{R}egion see\textbf{K}ing}, a training-free framework that turns this semantic guidance into targeted visual observations. Exploration probes describe relevant context and distinguishing target details, while verification probes identify evidence needed t
sf192459b5b.summary: SPARK is a training-free framework that uses VLM-generated semantic probes to guide adaptive region zooming for GUI grounding, even when coordinate predictions are wrong.
sf192459b5b.why: Offers a training-free way to improve GUI element localization for computer-use agents by leveraging VLM visual descriptions.

s1bd1d8d67e.title: Machine learning enables full Bayesian inference for spinning extreme-mass-ratio inspirals
s1bd1d8d67e.description: arXiv:2611.31916v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs), stellar-mass compact objects spiralling into massive black holes, promise to measure the masses and spins of the central black holes, reveal the strong-field environment around them and gauge cosmic distances via millihertz gravitational-wave observations. Yet most forecasts for the parameter inference of these systems assume known source parameters, and broad-prior analyses have addressed only simplified versions of the problem. The joint inversion of all 14 parameters of a spinning source from the complete prior has remained unsolved. Here we solve it for the augmented analytic kludge model: generative networks narrow the complete prior and reveal a ring of degenerate spin directions, and the exact de
s1bd1d8d67e.summary: Researchers report a machine learning method enabling full Bayesian inference over all 14 parameters of spinning extreme-mass-ratio inspirals from gravitational-wave data.

s56660a6cde.title: Beyond Rigid Hands: Deforming Skin into Contact-Consistent Hand Meshes
s56660a6cde.description: arXiv:2611.31950v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hands grasp objects with soft skin. A fingertip flattens against a mug, and a palm curves around a bottle. Yet hand-object datasets and estimators represent the hand as a rigid articulated mesh, which hovers above or penetrates the object where skin would press against it. Existing refiners keep the mesh rigid and adjust only the pose, trading pose accuracy for physical plausibility. We ask whether a rigid hand can instead touch the object as skin does while staying close to its original pose. We lift annotated or estimated rigid hands to contact-consistent meshes through an optimization that (i) slightly adjusts the joints and wrist to bring the fingers onto the object, (ii) deforms the skin so that penetrating regions settle onto the surf
s56660a6cde.summary: A paper presents a method that deforms rigid annotated or estimated hand meshes into skin-like, contact-consistent shapes that touch objects realistically while staying close to the original pose.

s88db3c59b7.title: Are Web Agents Still Detectable? Stress-Testing Bot Defenses with Coordinated Evasion
s88db3c59b7.description: arXiv:2611.31962v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI web agents can autonomously navigate websites and complete various tasks. As their capabilities and adoption expand, evaluating bot defenses requires adversarial stress tests. Although prior work demonstrates that existing agents can remain detectable, it remains unclear how effective bot defenses are against adversaries that coordinate evasion across browser fingerprints, automation controls, and interaction behavior. To investigate this threat, we introduce DarkAgent, an autonomous web agent that combines a forked Chromium browser that conceals automation artifacts and generative models that produce human-like mouse and keyboard traces. To address the limitations of existing keyboard mimickers, our keyboard model jointly generates real
s88db3c59b7.summary: DarkAgent, an autonomous web agent with a forked Chromium browser, is introduced to stress-test whether bot defenses can detect agents that coordinate evasion across fingerprints and behavior.
s88db3c59b7.why: Highlights that coordinated evasion may defeat current bot defenses, which matters for teams protecting sites from automated agents.

sce50909a9f.title: Distill to Loop: Turning Pretrained Diffusion Transformers into Looped Models with Adjustable Depth
sce50909a9f.description: arXiv:2611.31977v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Looped transformers reuse one block of shared weights along the depth of the network. Recent looped diffusion transformers are trained from scratch, which repeats the full pretraining cost although strong pretrained non-looped diffusion transformers exist. We propose Distill to Loop (Dooop), which distills a pretrained non-looped diffusion transformer into a looped student whose blocks are initialized from the teacher's. We cast distillation as a fixed-point iteration toward the teacher, in which the output after every loop is trained toward the teacher, and each loop is one step of an ordinary differential equation in depth. As a result, one model runs any number of loops at test time without retraining, and the higher-order ODE solvers of
sce50909a9f.summary: Distill to Loop (Dooop) distills a pretrained non-looped diffusion transformer into a looped student with adjustable depth, initializing blocks from the teacher.
sce50909a9f.why: Could cut the cost of building looped diffusion transformers by reusing existing pretrained non-looped models rather than training from scratch.

sf53641795b.title: Reading, Writing and Repairing Game-Theoretic Policies in Weight Space
sf53641795b.description: arXiv:2611.31979v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Can a language model work in the weight space of a policy network for a repeated game? We put four questions to a mid-size open model, on recurrent networks of 1{,}218 weights with exactly checkable answers. Given a population of opponents described in English, write a policy that is optimal: its value is a finite computation over the agent's information state, so a submitted network has an exact gap from the optimum. Given a network's weights, report its action after each of fifteen opponent histories; recover the state machine it implements, judged on every opponent sequence to depth ten; or repair a network whose output was altered in one place and say which round first goes wrong. The model recovers the program in 62 of 66 replies, repo
sf53641795b.summary: A study tests whether a mid-size open language model can write, read, and repair policy network weights for repeated games with exactly checkable answers.

s13d354bba6.title: ADE: A Zero-Training Unlearning Method for Latent World Models
s13d354bba6.description: arXiv:2611.31998v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Latent world models learn compact recurrent dynamics from offline trajectories, yet deployed simulators can retain backdoor triggers or stale transitions from outdated physical regimes. Existing unlearning methods fail in autoregressive physics: gradient updates distort latent manifolds and compound rollout drift, naive output zeroing suppresses valid control responses on trigger onset, and single-step deletion leaves corruption inside recurrent hidden states. We propose Analytical Dynamics Excision (ADE), a deterministic, zero-training closed-form unlearning algorithm for latent world models. Using only cached pretraining moments, ADE recovers retain covariances via single-pass matrix downdating without raw retain data and cascades closed-
s13d354bba6.summary: Analytical Dynamics Excision (ADE) is a deterministic, zero-training method for removing backdoor triggers and stale transitions from latent world models.
s13d354bba6.why: Offers a training-free unlearning approach for deployed learned simulators, avoiding the drift problems of gradient-based unlearning.

s6b4aa541a3.title: Calm Agent: Reframing Agent Interaction around Intermittent Human Attention
s6b4aa541a3.description: arXiv:2611.32009v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI agents can carry out auxiliary tasks while users focus on other work. Yet users still need to understand task state, make changes, and respond when help is required. We argue that agents for ongoing auxiliary tasks should be designed around intermittent human attention: tasks should continue between interactions, and users should be able to return with little effort to understand and control them. We develop this position as Calm Agent. It connects three on-demand interaction modes: Delegate, Adjust, and Check, through a persistent task representation. Generative interaction provides controls and feedback suited to open-ended goals, while existing controls support routine actions. We illustrate these principles with Orvlet, a desktop pro
s6b4aa541a3.summary: Calm Agent proposes designing agents for ongoing auxiliary tasks around intermittent human attention, with Delegate, Adjust, and Check interaction modes.
s6b4aa541a3.why: Offers a design framework for agent UX where users return intermittently, relevant to teams building long-running assistants.

s8ccb5f136e.title: To Critic Or Not To Critic
s8ccb5f136e.description: arXiv:2611.32013v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As large language models tackle longer and more complex tasks, understanding when a critic improves the efficiency of reinforcement learning (RL) becomes increasingly important. Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) trains a critic to reduce variance and provide fine-grained credit assignment, while Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) drops the critic and avoids the bias of bootstrapping from the critic's value estimates. Although recent critic-based methods have reported strong performance relative to GRPO, it remains unclear when each approach is preferable. We argue that there is no universal answer; instead, the choice depends on several interacting factors, including batch size, critic reliance, and task complexity. We study the bia
s8ccb5f136e.summary: A paper examines when a learned critic improves reinforcement learning efficiency for LLMs, comparing PPO with a critic against critic-free GRPO.
s8ccb5f136e.why: Helps teams choose between PPO and GRPO for LLM RL training based on task length and complexity.

s31db0a59f7.title: When Online Adaptation of Resilience Policies Hurts: Safe Exploration and Measurement Pitfalls in Resilience4j
s31db0a59f7.description: arXiv:2611.32015v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Circuit breaker, retry, and bulkhead settings in Java microservices are tuned once and frozen, although the best setting depends on the fault a dependency is currently showing. We study whether an online learner can pick these settings at runtime. AdaptR4j swaps Resilience4j policies atomically in Spring Boot 3 and lets a contextual bandit choose among complete CircuitBreaker/Retry/Bulkhead configurations from Prometheus signals. Our first, naive design scored worse than keeping the default policy in three of four winnable fault scenarios under the reward it optimised: exploring a menu that contained aggressive circuit breakers rejected most traffic while the learner was still learning. Two safeguards fix this: a safe policy menu (no breake
s31db0a59f7.summary: Researchers study whether an online contextual bandit can pick Resilience4j circuit breaker, retry, and bulkhead settings at runtime, finding naive adaptation sometimes underperformed defaults.
s31db0a59f7.why: Shows that runtime tuning of microservice resilience policies can backfire without careful safe exploration and measurement, relevant to SREs considering adaptive configs.

s1ee005c691.title: Structure-Aware Transformers for Hierarchical Authorization in Personal AI Agents
s1ee005c691.description: arXiv:2611.32018v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Personal AI agents can carry out complex, multi-step tasks on users' behalf, but doing so often involves numerous permission requests. Manually reviewing each request is time-consuming, while indiscriminate approval poses privacy and security risks. Predicting users' authorization preferences offers a way to reduce this burden while preserving user control. However, authorization prediction is challenging because permission requests are often hierarchical and observed user decisions are sparse and potentially correlated. To address these challenges, We propose the Parent-gated Authorization Transformer for Hierarchies (PATH) to predict users' authorization preferences for personal AI agents. PATH is a novel neural network architecture that
s1ee005c691.summary: Researchers propose structure-aware transformers to predict users' authorization preferences for hierarchical permission requests from personal AI agents.
s1ee005c691.why: Could reduce permission-review burden for agent deployments, though the abstract gives little detail on results or evaluation.

s124f2d0e0a.title: HuluOPD: Unifying Heterogeneous Medical Specialists into One Lightweight Model with Unlabeled Prompts
s124f2d0e0a.description: arXiv:2611.32021v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Specialist medical vision-language models (VLMs) are strong within their specialties but hard to unify: their training data are often private, and independently developed specialists cannot be assumed to share an architecture. Deploying these large models separately is costly. We present HuluOPD, an on-policy distillation recipe that unifies heterogeneous specialists into one lightweight VLM using only unlabeled prompts, without requiring reference answers or the specialists' training data. The lightweight model answers each prompt, and the specialist of the prompt's modality supervises its response; a continuation-aligned cross-tokenizer loss makes this possible even when they differ in architecture and tokenizer. We apply HuluOPD to five
s124f2d0e0a.summary: HuluOPD is a method that distills several heterogeneous medical specialist vision-language models into one lightweight model using only unlabeled prompts.
s124f2d0e0a.why: Offers a route to consolidate costly specialist medical VLMs into a single cheaper model without access to private training data.

sad178096b9.title: Beyond Before-and-After Images: Evaluating Temporal Grounding in a Lightweight VLM for Disaster Assessment
sad178096b9.description: arXiv:2611.32022v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bi-temporal satellite imagery is central to disaster assessment: deciding what was damaged requires comparing a pre-event scene with its post-event counterpart. A vision-language model (VLM) can nonetheless appear to answer change questions while relying mainly on the post-event image or on the prompt's temporal framing. We present a controlled diagnostic of temporal grounding and apply it to one lightweight VLM, InternVL3-2B, on DisasterM3: 1,659 optical and SAR image pairs from 41 events and nine disaster types, in event-disjoint partitions, with 9,031 reasoning questions. We compare post-only input, the true pre/post pair, the post image repeated twice, reversed image order, and an unrelated pre-event image. The true pair scores $+0.5$ a
sad178096b9.summary: A diagnostic study tests whether the lightweight InternVL3-2B vision-language model truly uses pre- and post-disaster satellite images for temporal damage assessment.
sad178096b9.why: Highlights that VLMs may answer change questions by relying on one image or prompt framing, a reliability concern for high-stakes remote sensing use.

s15737b9eaa.title: Do Occupancy World Models Really Follow Actions?
s15737b9eaa.description: arXiv:2611.32029v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Occupancy world models predict future 3D scenes conditioned on ego actions, yet their predictions may not faithfully follow the specified trajectory under counterfactual actions. Because driving datasets provide sparse coverage of alternative trajectories for each scene, existing models learn the spatial effect of ego motion implicitly from observed scene--trajectory combinations, which may entangle action effects with scene--trajectory correlations. We propose ReCast, an ego-trajectory-guided transformer that grounds future prediction in action-induced geometric correspondence across ego-centric frames. ReCast decouples historical encoding from future decoding and aligns deformable interactions using relative ego transformations, while ret
s15737b9eaa.summary: ReCast, an ego-trajectory-guided transformer, is proposed to make occupancy world models follow specified actions under counterfactual driving trajectories.
s15737b9eaa.why: Addresses whether driving world models actually respond to action inputs, which matters for their use in planning and simulation.

s75bc0154ef.title: Unifying Partner and Environment Diversity to Improve Human-AI Coordination
s75bc0154ef.description: arXiv:2611.32031v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Real-world applications of modern AI systems require generalization to both unseen environments and novel human users. The field of zero-shot coordination (ZSC) has focused primarily on deploying AI to cooperate with novel partners in otherwise familiar environments. Popular population-based methods achieve this by partnering the agent with a diversity of simulated human users during training in a fixed environment, but does not consider the more realistic scenario where both the users and the environment are unseen during training. Recently, training across environments has been explored in training a single self-play agent, which shows better generalization on both novel human users and unseen environments. In this work, we ask whether jo
s75bc0154ef.summary: Researchers propose a method combining partner and environment diversity to improve zero-shot human-AI coordination when both users and environments are unseen.
s75bc0154ef.why: Targets generalization to new users and settings, a practical requirement for deployed cooperative AI, though the abstract is brief on results.

sba37971e15.title: Provenance-Isolated Epistemic Quorums: Execution-Bound Evidence Certification and Plausible-World Safety Gating in Agentic Control Planes
sba37971e15.description: arXiv:2611.32032v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agreement among large language models is not physical evidence for mutating production infrastructure. Because generative models share pretraining priors and conform to peer rationales during deliberation, voting ensembles correlate errors instead of providing independent fault tolerance; yet attaching rigid deterministic checks to unconstrained agent outputs paralyzes incident remediation. We present Provenance-Isolated Epistemic Quorums (PIEQ), an execution-bound certification layer that keeps every language model strictly outside the trusted computing base. PIEQ unifies assumption-based truth maintenance, physical provenance isolation, control-theoretic plausible-world safety shielding, and linearizable concurrency governance around thre
sba37971e15.summary: PIEQ, a certification layer, is presented that keeps language models outside the trusted path and gates mutating production infrastructure actions on execution-bound evidence.
sba37971e15.why: Argues LLM agreement is not evidence for production changes, a design concern for teams letting agents perform incident remediation.

s06aa91feda.title: Spec-CoFrGeNet: Reparametrizing Continued Fraction Networks for Stable and Accurate Training
s06aa91feda.description: arXiv:2611.32041v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Continued fractions have been shown to be a function class capable of constructing expressive yet parameter-efficient neural networks. These neural networks are not only effective for supervised learning, but also for training LLMs. However, the rational form of this function class introduces poles when the denominator approaches zero, which prior work has avoided by enforcing a small positive (non-smooth) lower bound. We show that performance and training stability can be highly sensitive to the choice of this lower bound. In this work, we introduce a novel transformation of the partial denominators, inspired by its connection to the Green's function in physics, that mitigates the above issue elegantly by constraining the spectra of the co
s06aa91feda.summary: Spec-CoFrGeNet reparametrizes continued fraction networks to improve training stability and accuracy, including for LLM training, by addressing denominator pole issues.
s06aa91feda.why: Shows training stability can be highly sensitive to a lower-bound choice, a practical tuning detail for this architecture class.

s88446f2a86.title: Integral DeltaNet: Improved Linear Attention with Adaptive Memory Integration
s88446f2a86.description: arXiv:2611.32063v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Linear attention replaces softmax attention with a linear formulation, enabling linear-time computation with a fixed-size recurrent state instead of a growing key-value cache. These computational and memory advantages have attracted growing interest in linear attention for long-context language modeling. However, compressing past information into a fixed-size state causes memory collisions that hinder long-context understanding. Although DeltaNet mitigates memory collisions through delta-rule updates and Gated DeltaNet extends this approach with gating, these mechanisms may also discard information relevant to future predictions. To address this limitation, we introduce Integral DeltaNet, which maintains two complementary recurrent states:
s88446f2a86.summary: Integral DeltaNet is proposed as an improved linear attention method using adaptive memory integration to reduce memory collisions in long-context modeling.
s88446f2a86.why: Targets a known weakness of fixed-size linear attention states for long-context language models, relevant to efficiency-focused architecture choices.

s201608d0a6.title: The algorithmic behavioral sink: Modeling the transition to irreversible demographic collapse
s201608d0a6.description: arXiv:2611.32084v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In 2025, the vast majority of major global economies reported a Total Fertility Rate below the replacement level of 2.1. This synchronized collapse has persisted despite extensive pro-natalist financial interventions, revealing a structural limitation in conventional linear demographic models. This paper proposes that the ubiquity of mobile internet and Artificial Intelligence acts as a synthetic mating disruptor, precipitating a non-linear phase transition in human pair-bonding dynamics. Treating the marriage market as a complex system governed by thermodynamic constraints, we present a Fermi-Dirac selection model, using national income distributions as the input spectrum and fitted with Japanese longitudinal data to illustrate how digital
s201608d0a6.summary: A paper models mobile internet and AI as a synthetic mating disruptor, proposing a non-linear phase transition toward irreversible demographic collapse.

s6ee3f4f03f.title: MARGIN: A Risk-Aware Agent for Robot Program Refinement
s6ee3f4f03f.description: arXiv:2611.32093v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Robot-programming agents improve executable control policies through repeated testing and repair, yet binary success saturates while execution risk persists across unseen scenes. We introduce MARGIN, a risk-aware agent that converts successful robot rollouts into actionable evidence for program refinement. Its near-miss margin measures the fraction of the execution budget remaining in the slowest successful development rollout. The agent uses this signal to prioritize fragile programs, guide targeted repairs, and select revisions that preserve development success while increasing execution headroom. An exact safe-racing rule accelerates success-based candidate evaluation. We evaluate MARGIN across LIBERO-Pro, LIBERO-90, and Robosuite. In ou
s6ee3f4f03f.summary: MARGIN is a risk-aware robot-programming agent that uses a near-miss margin signal to prioritize fragile programs and guide targeted repairs.
s6ee3f4f03f.why: Shows using execution-risk signals beyond binary success to refine robot control programs, relevant to robotics teams testing across unseen scenes.

s08d3b54c51.title: Clinical3D-Bench: Evaluating and Improving Spatial Intelligence of Multimodal LLMs in Hospital Environments
s08d3b54c51.description: arXiv:2611.32094v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spatial reasoning in hospitals requires tracking look-alike equipment, interpreting patient-relative directions, and judging passage widths, yet existing benchmarks provide limited coverage of these abilities. We introduce Clinical3D-Bench, a simulated benchmark with 3,368 questions of eight types on egocentric walkthroughs of 373 hospital-room layouts. Layouts follow hospital design guidelines, answers are computed from the 3D scenes, and paired scene states test whether models change their answers when relevant evidence changes. Videos are photorealistic, and ten physicians screened the layouts. Among 35 multimodal large language models (MLLMs), the best open and proprietary models reach 45.7% and 53.6% macro accuracy, against 40.8% for a
s08d3b54c51.summary: Clinical3D-Bench is a simulated benchmark with 3,368 questions on hospital-room walkthroughs to evaluate spatial intelligence of multimodal LLMs.
s08d3b54c51.why: Provides a targeted benchmark for spatial reasoning in clinical environments, useful for teams assessing embodied or assistive models in hospitals.

s34f825354a.title: PreferenceScene: Personalized Indoor Scene Synthesis from Feedback
s34f825354a.description: arXiv:2611.32099v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Text-to-scene methods turn a short instruction into a furnished 3D room, but the room that a particular person wants rarely comes across fully in words: many preferences surface only when the person sees a concrete room and can point to what they like and dislike in it. We therefore study personalized indoor scene synthesis under hidden user preferences: over several turns, a system shows a 3D scene, and the user, who sees only rendered images of the scene, replies with brief free-form feedback and a satisfaction score. The system must therefore bring the whole room toward the user's preferences from feedback that comments on only part of it at a time. It must also be able to change every part of the room, because a preference concerns not
s34f825354a.summary: PreferenceScene proposes personalized indoor scene synthesis that learns hidden user preferences from multi-turn free-form feedback and satisfaction scores on rendered 3D rooms.
s34f825354a.why: Demonstrates interactive preference elicitation for generative 3D content, though the abstract gives little on results.

s786666eee3.title: Duo: Towards Spatiotemporal Action Coordination in Bimanual Policies
s786666eee3.description: arXiv:2611.32108v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bimanual manipulation requires each arm to perform distinct motions while coordinating with the other. Common flow-based robotic policies combine both arms' actions into one token per future timestep, giving attention distinct positions across time but not across arms. We introduce Duo, a simple but effective design that models spatial and temporal dependencies within one shared action head. Specifically, Duo separates both arms into two action tokens per timestep, allowing each arm's motion to interact via cross-arm attention during flow matching. On RoboTwin 2.0, Duo improves the overall success of all four base policies, from 0.45B to 3.62B parameters, with gains of 12.55 and 9.02 percentage points for FLOWER (0.89B) and $\pi_{0.5}$ (3.6
s786666eee3.summary: Duo is a bimanual robot policy design that splits each arm into its own action token per timestep, enabling cross-arm attention within a shared action head.
s786666eee3.why: Offers an architectural change for coordinated two-arm manipulation policies, relevant to robotics teams building flow-based policies.

s4987f1f082.title: An Automated Framework Integrating Deep Learning and Anatomical Reasoning for Cardiac Phenotyping From CCTA
s4987f1f082.description: arXiv:2611.32114v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) depicts coronary anatomy and cardiac fat, but segmentation alone does not ensure anatomically consistent measurements. We propose an automated framework that combines deep learning with anatomical reasoning for quantitative cardiac phenotyping. Its anatomical measurement module uses graph geometry, branch identity, and surrounding structures to define vessel-specific pericoronary adipose tissue (PCAT) sampling and a surrogate epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) compartment. The latter also generates training targets without requiring expert pericardium contours. A companion module quantifies coronary calcium on non-contrast CT. Component-wise benchmarking was conducted on five public datasets: Ima
s4987f1f082.summary: Researchers present an automated framework combining deep learning with anatomical reasoning to quantify pericoronary and epicardial fat from cardiac CCTA scans.
s4987f1f082.why: Shows how adding anatomical constraints can yield more consistent clinical measurements than segmentation alone, relevant to medical imaging pipelines.

sced2e4a964.title: VIDE : Training-Free Video Anomaly Detection via Visual Intrinsic Distribution Estimation
sced2e4a964.description: arXiv:2611.32138v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In embedding-based video anomaly detection (VAD), normal clips can have high similarity to anomalous descriptions, an anomaly bias that leads to false positives. Methods such as PRISM mitigate this bias by measuring deviations from a normality reference along anomaly directions. Both the normality reference and the anomaly directions are derived from text and shared across videos, although normal activity and the appearance of anomalies vary across scenes. The resulting scores are also sensitive to prompt selection. To address these limitations, we propose Visual Intrinsic Distribution Estimation (VIDE), a training-free framework that adapts text-derived scoring to each test video using frozen clip embeddings. VIDE estimates normal scene co
sced2e4a964.summary: VIDE proposes a training-free video anomaly detection method that estimates visual intrinsic distributions to reduce the false positives caused by anomaly bias in embedding-based approaches.
sced2e4a964.why: Training-free anomaly detection that adapts to each scene's normal activity could reduce false alarms without costly retraining for video surveillance systems.

sbca174bc1c.title: Calibrated Reading of Latent Reasoning and Communication
sbca174bc1c.description: arXiv:2611.32143v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Latent reasoning and key-value communication store intermediate information in continuous representations, limiting direct inspection of model behavior. Existing activation readers trade the low cost of task-specific probes against the flexibility of language-model decoders. We propose the Calibrated Latent Reader, CLR, a compact transformer that predicts reasoning outcomes and message content through task-conditioned interactions between states and candidate answers. Source adapters support transfer across models, while conformal calibration provides coverage and false-alarm guarantees under exchangeability. On two CODI models, CLR improves accuracy over MLP and attention probes by 4-18 percentage points for final-answer prediction and ref
sbca174bc1c.summary: Researchers introduce the Calibrated Latent Reader (CLR), a compact transformer that predicts reasoning outcomes and message content from latent model states, with conformal calibration.
sbca174bc1c.why: Offers a cheaper, more flexible way to inspect latent reasoning and key-value communication in models, aiding debugging and transparency.

seb4090b99e.title: RetraQ: Manifold-Constrained Critic Guidance for Flow Policies in RL
seb4090b99e.description: arXiv:2611.32148v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A learned critic can improve a pretrained flow-matching policy by steering sampled actions toward higher predicted value. However, even a critic that fits the behavior data well can provide misleading action gradients. Gradient components pointing away from the data-supported region are weakly constrained by behavior data and can lead guidance to exploit critic extrapolation errors. We introduce RetraQ (Retraction-based Q-guidance), which uses geometry encoded by the pretrained flow to constrain both the direction and the destination of critic guidance. A single velocity evaluation of the frozen flow defines a denoising map. RetraQ filters the critic gradient with the map's Jacobian and applies the map itself to correct the updated action.
seb4090b99e.summary: RetraQ is a method that uses pretrained flow geometry to constrain critic-guided action gradients, aiming to keep flow-matching RL policies within data-supported regions.
seb4090b99e.why: Addresses critic extrapolation errors when steering flow-matching policies, which matters for teams applying offline RL to robotics or control.

s34631157b3.title: Making Evaluation Explicit Is Not Enough: Supervising the Evaluation Process in Generative Reward Models
s34631157b3.description: arXiv:2611.32161v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative reward models (GRMs) make language-model evaluation more explicit by generating critiques, rubrics, or intermediate analyses before predicting a final preference. However, explicit evaluation does not necessarily imply a reliable evaluation process: under outcome-only supervision, a model may reach the correct final preference while producing weak or unsupported intermediate judgments, turning the evaluation into a post-hoc rationalization. We introduce STEP-GRM, a framework that directly supervises the intermediate evaluation process of rubric-based GRMs. In addition to conventional preference supervision, STEP-GRM provides structural guidance for rubric construction and local supervision for criterion-level judgments, encouragi
s34631157b3.summary: STEP-GRM is a framework that directly supervises the intermediate evaluation steps of generative reward models, rather than only final preference outcomes.
s34631157b3.why: Suggests outcome-only training can yield unsupported intermediate judgments, a concern for teams relying on LLM-as-judge evaluation pipelines.

s9d4c2eb4dd.title: RightDiff: Learning Generative Reward Models to Judge by the Right Differences
s9d4c2eb4dd.description: arXiv:2611.32166v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative reward models typically rely on generic query-level rubrics or unconstrained rationales, overlooking the fact that pairwise preference is driven by response-specific differences. Moreover, optimizing solely for outcome correctness encourages models to exploit superficial shortcuts such as verbosity and formatting, triggering rationale drift. To address this, we propose RightDiff, which structures pairwise evaluation into an evidence-grounded evaluation trajectory executed in a single autoregressive generation. RightDiff explicitly discovers contrastive differences between candidates, categorizes them into material or immaterial factors, and induces pair-specific rubrics before final adjudication. To train this process without pos
s9d4c2eb4dd.summary: RightDiff is a generative reward model that structures pairwise evaluation around response-specific differences in a single autoregressive pass to reduce shortcut exploitation.
s9d4c2eb4dd.why: Targets verbosity and formatting shortcuts in LLM judges, relevant for teams building reliable automated preference evaluation.

s42ff764dde.title: Benchmarking Protein Structure Tokenizers as Generation Targets for Language Models
s42ff764dde.description: arXiv:2611.32168v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Discrete structure tokenizers are the standard way to give a language model access to protein three-dimensional structure, yet they are selected on how accurately they can be read, their reconstruction fidelity, while the property that governs generation is how well a model can write them. We measure this property, writability, directly: holding the base model, data, recipe and compute fixed, we swap only the tokenizer and train the same 9B model to emit structure tokens residue by residue, over eight tokenizers, four compute budgets and three evaluation sets (96 cells). At 2B tokens final writability runs from TM 0.662 down to 0.378 under identical conditions, with five of the eight arms clearing the TM 0.5 mark at which a fold is usually
s42ff764dde.summary: The paper benchmarks eight protein structure tokenizers by training the same 9B model to generate structure tokens, measuring how well each tokenizer can be written by a language model.
s42ff764dde.why: Shows reconstruction fidelity is not the property that governs generation, which matters for teams choosing tokenizers for protein language models.

s8772181721.title: Mind the Band: The Hidden Frequency Variable in Geometric RoPE
s8772181721.description: arXiv:2611.32171v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Geometric rotary position encodings (RoPE) incorporate 3D camera geometry into multi-view attention by rotating token features according to viewing rays, depths, and reprojected image coordinates. Each coordinate is rotated across a progression of frequencies--its frequency band--yet existing implementations leave this band to inherited defaults, either retaining standard 2D RoPE's top frequency or letting the frequency span grow exponentially with the attention head dimension. We show that this unstandardized setting can reverse benchmark rankings. In novel view synthesis on RealEstate10K, RayRoPE matches the strongest baseline in the 47M model (144-channel heads), yet trails by 1.2 dB in the 25M model (48-channel heads), and exhibits the
s8772181721.summary: The paper shows that unstandardized frequency bands in geometric RoPE for multi-view attention can reverse benchmark rankings, and examines this hidden variable.
s8772181721.why: Implementation defaults for positional encodings can silently change benchmark results, so teams comparing multi-view models should standardize them.

sf38fc13b4c.title: DocPristine: Content-Aware Document Appearance Enhancement under Real-World Mixed Degradations
sf38fc13b4c.description: arXiv:2611.32176v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Camera-captured documents often exhibit mixed degradations, such as highlights, shadows, and blur, that distort backgrounds and obscure text details. Document appearance enhancement (DAE) aims to mitigate these degradations and improve readability. Existing document appearance enhancement methods rely either on input-derived visual cues that can become unreliable under severe degradation or on LLM-based degradation diagnosis that lacks spatial guidance. Notably, we find that pretrained document visual encoders continue to attend to text regions in degraded documents, providing content-aware guidance. Based on this insight, we propose DocPristine, which adaptively fuses multi-layer features from a frozen document visual encoder and injects t
sf38fc13b4c.summary: DocPristine is a content-aware document appearance enhancement method that targets mixed real-world degradations such as highlights, shadows, and blur in camera-captured documents.
sf38fc13b4c.why: Addresses document image cleanup under combined degradations, relevant for teams building OCR or document ingestion pipelines.

sb0ac2249d7.title: ThinkMorph-SSL: Scaling Interleaved Multimodal Reasoning with Pretext Tasks
sb0ac2249d7.description: arXiv:2611.32183v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: People reason with pictures as well as words. Interleaved multimodal reasoning gives models a similar way to solve problems by creating intermediate images and using them to guide further reasoning. Training models with this ability usually relies on task-specific demonstrations, which are difficult to collect. We introduce ThinkMorph-SSL, a two-stage training recipe that uses images themselves as a source of supervision. The first stage, pretext reasoning, converts visual pretext tasks, such as image colorization and denoising, into instruction-free interleaved traces. Models describe a corrupted or transformed image, generate a restored or canonical image, and interpret the result. The second stage uses automatically constructed demonstra
sb0ac2249d7.summary: ThinkMorph-SSL is a two-stage training recipe that uses image pretext tasks like colorization and denoising to supervise interleaved multimodal reasoning without task-specific demonstrations.
sb0ac2249d7.why: Reduces reliance on hard-to-collect demonstrations for training models that reason through intermediate images.

s2637157992.title: Blaming the Machine, Billing the Victim? How Mock Jurors Reassign Fault from Generative AI Systems and Respond to Liability Cliffs in Tort
s2637157992.description: arXiv:2611.32188v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative AI complicates tort liability attribution when people blame a generative AI system that cannot itself bear legally relevant fault. We investigate where this blame goes when fault must be allocated among legal persons, and whether American discontinuous apportionment doctrines influence mock jurors' factual findings of fault. Such doctrines include Contributory negligence, Joint and several liability, and their 50% or 51% variations, all of which have a fault-percentage threshold or a "cliff" where the victim-entitled compensation (or a defendant's liability) jumps to zero (or to all compensatory damages). Our pre-registered human subjects experiment (N=199 Prolific participants) shows that as many U.S. mock jurors (36%) blame the
s2637157992.summary: A study of mock jurors examines how they reassign fault from generative AI systems to legal persons and how contributory negligence and joint liability thresholds affect findings.
s2637157992.why: Shows how liability doctrines may shape blame allocation involving AI systems, relevant for legal and risk planning for AI deployers.

s6a94137cb0.title: SolarFilNet-V4: Multi-Scale Transformer Vision with Physics-Informed Adaptive Post-Processing for Solar Filament Segmentation
s6a94137cb0.description: arXiv:2611.32193v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Solar filaments are cool, dense chromospheric plasma structures held by magnetic field lines above polarity inversion lines. Their destabilization triggers coronal mass ejections and severe space weather hazards. Segmenting individual filaments from ground-based GONG H-alpha observations (2048 x 2048 pixels) is challenging due to low contrast, turbulent fibrils, delicate barb structures, and annotator boundary variance. In this technical report, we describe SolarFilNet-V4, a targeted segmentation framework developed for the MAGFiLO 1.0 benchmark (Solar Filament Segmentation Challenge 2026). Our method couples a lightweight Pyramid Vision Transformer (PVT-v2-B1) backbone with anisotropic curvilinear strip convolutions (k=15) and dual-frequen
s6a94137cb0.summary: SolarFilNet-V4 is a multi-scale transformer segmentation framework with physics-informed post-processing for segmenting solar filaments in GONG H-alpha observations.

s86c63cf108.title: LLM Agent Authorization Across Context Compaction
s86c63cf108.description: arXiv:2611.32194v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Request-derived authorizers such as Progent protect LLM agents from prompt injection by deriving what an agent may do from the user's request. Their guarantee rests on attribution: the request is taken to be what the user said. Compaction breaks it. At every automatic compaction we observed, Claude Code and Codex placed a model-written summary of earlier turns as a user message, so the compactor's quotation of the user, documents and injected text reads as the user speaking. Because a policy frozen at the first request lets the agent finish few later tasks, we let Progent derive its policy for each request, and find that what it grants then follows what the compactor wrote. Even a payee the user stated is not safe: when an attacker's notice
s86c63cf108.summary: The paper shows that request-derived authorization for LLM agents breaks during automatic context compaction, because summaries of earlier turns are placed as user messages in Claude Code and Codex.
s86c63cf108.why: Reveals a prompt-injection gap in agent authorization, so teams running coding agents with compaction should not assume request-based policies remain enforced.

sa940e2c5f4.title: When Answering Is Administering: Permission Replies That Rewrite Coding-Agent Policy
sa940e2c5f4.description: arXiv:2611.32195v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coding agents let plugins and remote services answer permission prompts, and Claude Code documents that such an answer cannot override the operator's deny rules. However, we show that this guarantee, checked one decision at a time, fails over a whole run, because an answer to one permission prompt can rewrite the policy that every later answer is checked against. For example, a remote service with no access to the operator's files approves an unrelated command and attaches an update that deletes the deny rule protecting the project's secrets. The agent then reads the secrets in that session and the next, even inside the vendor's strict sandbox. The root cause is that Claude Code checks only updates that add or replace allow rules. Relays th
sa940e2c5f4.summary: The paper shows that permission replies to coding agents can rewrite the policy checked on later decisions, letting a remote service delete deny rules across a run.
sa940e2c5f4.why: Demonstrates that per-decision permission checks can fail over a whole run, a concrete risk for teams granting plugins or remote services approval rights.

sad7f78b9d9.title: Steerable by Design: Conditional Pretraining for Robust Control of Language Models
sad7f78b9d9.description: arXiv:2611.32199v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Our goal is to build language models that are steerable by design. Today's language models are pretrained with next-token prediction, which relegates alignment and control to the final 1% of training tokens or inference-time interventions. These models repurpose a single input channel for both instructions and data, leading to common failure modes where the model mistakenly treats data as instructions such as intentional jailbreaks and unintentional in-context alignment drift. To correct this, we propose a pretraining method and architecture that separates the two from the very start, producing Mancelle-3B. An encoder processes high-level semantic features of upcoming text with cross-attention that prevents the token stream from writing bac
sad7f78b9d9.summary: The paper proposes a conditional pretraining method and architecture that separates instructions from data so language models are steerable by design rather than only aligned at the end.
sad7f78b9d9.why: Aims to reduce jailbreaks and in-context alignment drift by separating instruction and data channels during pretraining.

s98e5f4cc75.title: Who gets the information? An $\alpha$-fair label-coverage framework for multi-label feature selection
s98e5f4cc75.description: arXiv:2611.32200v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent information-theoretic filters for multi-label feature selection disagree on how to distribute relevance over labels: some amplify features that inform a few labels, others balance what every label receives. We show these choices are implicit social welfare functions. Treating labels as agents whose utility is the information they receive, we propose FLIC, which greedily maximises the $\alpha$-fair welfare of per-label information coverage. A single parameter $\alpha$ moves from utilitarian ($\alpha=0$) through proportionally fair ($\alpha=1$) to max-min selection ($\alpha\to\infty$), and a dozen published relevance terms lie on this axis, most as special cases, first-order approximations or limits. The objective is monotone submodula
s98e5f4cc75.summary: FLIC is an alpha-fair label-coverage framework for multi-label feature selection that treats labels as agents whose information utility is balanced via a welfare function.
s98e5f4cc75.why: Offers a tunable fairness parameter for feature selection across labels, though its practical impact for engineering teams is limited.

s1c2cab2037.title: OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval
s1c2cab2037.description: arXiv:2611.32203v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal retrieval must match dense pages, fine-grained entities, ordered video, and agent tools and memory. Single-vector embeddings lose local evidence, cross-encoders reread every recalled item online, and uncompressed late interaction is too large to serve. We present OmniEVIE, a 4.5B multi-vector embedding model covering text, images, visual documents, video, and tools with one compressed index and a three-stage retriever. Each record stores at most 128 int8 vectors of dimension 64 (9,472 bytes, or 8.82 GiB per million records), providing a mean vector, 1-bit signs, and int8 multi-vectors for coarse, middle, and final search while localizing each hit to a page region or video interval. Training, merging, indexing, and retrieval are c
s1c2cab2037.summary: OmniEVIE is a 4.5B multi-vector embedding model covering text, images, visual documents, video, and tools, using one compressed index and a three-stage retriever.
s1c2cab2037.why: It offers a compressed multi-vector approach to multimodal retrieval, aiming to keep local evidence while remaining cheap enough to serve at scale.

s3b65fc2005.title: Joint Classification and Generation on Tabular Data: an Empirical Study
s3b65fc2005.description: arXiv:2611.32225v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many applications of machine learning on tabular data need both a classifier and a generator of realistic records. The default is to train two separate models, whereas a single joint model promises both from one set of weights. Several families of tabular deep learning models can be turned into such a joint model, which raises the question of which joint model is preferable at which computational budget. In this empirical study, we introduce and compare joint models based on four state-of-the-art tabular data modeling families (energy-based models, probabilistic circuits, tabular foundation models and tabular diffusion models) against measured FLOPs and wall-clock time, on 29 classification datasets. Methods are evaluated based on two defin
s3b65fc2005.summary: Researchers present an empirical study comparing joint models that both classify and generate realistic tabular records, built from four tabular deep learning families.
s3b65fc2005.why: It informs whether one shared model can replace two separate classifier and generator models at a given compute budget.

sf53e2cf979.title: Roboclock: A Unified Benchmark for Time-Aware Robotic Intelligence
sf53e2cf979.description: arXiv:2611.32233v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Time is a fundamental dimension of robotic intelligence: a robot may fail despite physically correct actions if it acts outside a valid time window, responds too slowly to an event, or fails to meet required throughput. Yet existing robotic benchmarks primarily emphasize spatial correctness and logical task completion, largely overlooking the temporal constraints of real-world applications. We present RoboClock, a unified benchmark for time-aware robotic manipulation featuring 60 tasks across five application domains. Mirroring these failure modes, RoboClock structures tasks around three types of temporal constraints: Temporal Window, Event-Reactive, and Throughput. Furthermore, RoboClock incorporates a Latency-Aligned evaluation protocol t
sf53e2cf979.summary: Researchers introduced RoboClock, a benchmark with 60 tasks across five domains that tests time-aware robotic manipulation, including temporal constraints.
sf53e2cf979.why: Current robotics benchmarks overlook timing constraints, so this gives teams a way to test throughput and response-time failures.

sa8b12218dc.title: Boundary-Aware Policy Learning for Agent-Orchestrated Robot Manipulation
sa8b12218dc.description: arXiv:2611.32238v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agent-orchestrated robot systems combine the general reasoning capability of multimodal agents with the precise physical control of learned visuomotor policies. Yet such systems often fail at the moment of handoff: a policy is reliable only from a limited set of start states, while the agent may invoke it outside this region. We call this region the policy's handoff boundary. Existing whole-task policies typically have handoff boundaries that are narrow and difficult for an agent to characterize, making reliable coordination challenging. We propose Boundary-Aware Policy Learning, which explicitly shapes and then expands the handoff boundary of a visuomotor policy. First, Boundary-Explicit Training fine-tunes the policy on contact segments w
sa8b12218dc.summary: Researchers propose boundary-aware policy learning to address handoff failures when an agent invokes a robot manipulation policy outside its reliable start states.
sa8b12218dc.why: Handoff failures between agents and learned visuomotor policies are a practical reliability problem for agent-orchestrated robot systems.

s536e8407fd.title: CoMNO: Commutator Memory Neural Operators for Long-Horizon PDE Prediction
s536e8407fd.description: arXiv:2611.32274v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Solving nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) over long time horizons is computationally expensive using traditional numerical methods. While neural operators provide an efficient alternative, they suffer from the accumulation of approximation errors along the predicted trajectory, typically caused by the failure to capture fine-scale details. In this work, we design a Commutator Memory Neural Operator that identifies fine-scale dynamical details by commuting two operations and leverages these details to enhance the neural operator's capability in capturing fine-scale features over long time horizons. Specifically, we identify a performance gap between two operations: downsampling the high-resolution field before rollout predictio
s536e8407fd.summary: Researchers present CoMNO, a Commutator Memory Neural Operator designed to reduce error accumulation in long-horizon nonlinear PDE predictions.
s536e8407fd.why: Neural operators that stay accurate over long horizons could make PDE simulation cheaper than traditional numerical methods.

s99502c3ca2.title: Reproducing the Speech Labels of Qwen3-Omni's Talker: Mimi in bf16, and a Last-Frame Pitfall
s99502c3ca2.description: arXiv:2611.32286v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Qwen3-Omni speaks through a Talker predicting 16 codebooks of a 12.5 Hz audio codec, but the encoder that made its training labels was not released, so new voices cannot be trained on matching labels. We identify this encoder from the released model's behavior. White-box regression shows that the codebook embeddings of the Talker, its multi-token predictor and the Code2Wav decoder match the first 16 codebooks of kyutai's Mimi layer by layer.
