We call this the potentiality principle of foundation models: the base model already contains the capacity needed for task-specif
s5c6f25d5a7.summary: Researchers decompose foundation model adaptations into a shared input-independent component and a residual, finding the shared part accounts for most adaptation gains.
s5c6f25d5a7.why: Suggests much of fine-tuning gain may come from a simple learnable shift, potentially enabling cheaper adaptation methods.

sf1873fb0e8.title: One, No One and One Hundred Thousand CTs: Testing Anatomical Control in Text-to-CT Generation
sf1873fb0e8.description: arXiv:2611.33003v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent advances in deep learning and the public availability of computed tomography (CT) datasets with paired reports have enabled many Text-to-CT generators. However, their evaluations almost always differ in preprocessing and metrics, which hinders comparison. Moreover, their protocols almost never test how editing the report changes the CT, not even at the same seed, so the report is often assumed to control the anatomy without evidence of how much and how consistently it does. We therefore propose CtrlCT, a toolkit that tests two properties of a generator, Credibility and Control. Credibility tests compare generated CTs, as a population, with real CTs and reports; Control tests are metamorphic and need no reference CT: at a fixed seed,
sf1873fb0e8.summary: Researchers introduce CtrlCT, a toolkit that standardizes evaluation of text-to-CT generators and tests whether report edits consistently change the generated anatomy.
sf1873fb0e8.why: Provides a common evaluation protocol for medical text-to-CT generators, though the source text gives limited detail on results.

s6c7e3e2421.title: LEGOSpec: A Composable and Efficient Framework for Speculative Draft Design and Training
s6c7e3e2421.description: arXiv:2611.33004v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model (LLM) generation using a lightweight draft. Existing methods evaluate complete recipes under different training configurations, leaving component effects, interactions, and composition benefits unclear. Therefore, we present LEGOSpec, a composable framework for speculative draft design and training. LEGOSpec decomposes draft models into Context, Backbone, Proposal, and Objective components that share a unified training infrastructure. Using LEGOSpec, we systematically vary components and evaluate selected combinations under matched training conditions to isolate their effects and interactions. These experiments reveal three findings: (1) Different workloads favor different backbones, dep
s6c7e3e2421.summary: Researchers present LEGOSpec, a composable framework that decomposes speculative decoding draft models into Context, Backbone, Proposal, and Objective components for systematic study.
s6c7e3e2421.why: Helps engineers understand how individual draft-model design choices affect speculative decoding speed, though specific results are not in the provided text.

se274ec7e3c.title: Embodied AI Fails the Mirror Test: How a Simple Mirror Breaks Robot Policies
se274ec7e3c.description: arXiv:2611.33010v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Can a simple mirror expose the limitations of today's robotic manipulation policies? Inspired by the mirror self-recognition test in animal cognition, we investigate whether robot policies can reliably manipulate physical objects in scenes containing their reflections. We introduce RoboDojo-Mirror, a benchmark built on RoboDojo that preserves task objectives, success criteria, and policy checkpoints while comparing a mirror-free baseline with single-mirror, dual-mirror, and mirrored-tabletop conditions. Across five policies spanning Vision-Language-Action models, World Action Models, and agentic policies, every mirror condition reduces aggregate success rates: averaged over the three conditions, the drop ranges from 10.8 to 56.7 percentage
se274ec7e3c.summary: Researchers introduce RoboDojo-Mirror, a benchmark showing that adding mirrors to scenes causes five robot manipulation policies to perform worse.
se274ec7e3c.why: Reveals that common robot policies are brittle to reflections, a failure mode teams should test before deploying manipulation systems.

s2164a3d31d.title: Can a Frontier LLM Repair a Quantized Network by Tool-Free Weight-Space Programming?
s2164a3d31d.description: arXiv:2611.33031v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give four large language models (LLMs) of the Claude family the complete weights of a 20k-parameter CIFAR-10 CNN as text and ask them to produce a 4-bit network without tools, data or the ability to run inference. Standard round-to-nearest (RTN) quantization to 4 bit lowers the test accuracy from 81.4% to 60.4%. We design four evaluation protocols that differ in the input and task description given to the LLMs and analyze their responses. In the first two protocols the LLMs are given the float and the 4-bit RTN network and are told that the accuracy has dropped significantly. In the last two they receive only the float network and the task to quantize it, which tests whether they apply an optimization on their own or fall back to plain R
s2164a3d31d.summary: Researchers tested whether four Claude-family LLMs could convert a CIFAR-10 CNN's weights to a 4-bit network without tools, where round-to-nearest quantization drops accuracy from 81.4% to 60.4%.
s2164a3d31d.why: Probes the limits of LLMs reasoning directly over model weights, a question relevant to quantization and model compression workflows.

s570b39bfa8.title: AI is straining America’s open records systems
s570b39bfa8.description: In Panton, Vermont, population 660, town clerk Kyle Rowe did it all. He crafted budgets, paid vendors, handled property tax disputes, and served as the town’s zoning supervisor and presiding elections officer. During morning office hours at the town hall—a wood-frame structure built as a church in 1858—he also fielded public records requests. Recently, he…
s570b39bfa8.summary: AI is straining America's open records systems, using the example of a small Vermont town clerk handling public records requests alongside many other duties.
s570b39bfa8.why: Highlights rising AI-driven records request volume that strains under-resourced government systems, relevant to public-sector deployments.
